item.title: Google stock plunges as Q3 sales fall short of expectations
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Google stock plunges as Q3 sales fall short of expectations
2026-10-29
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/google-stock-plunges-as-q3-sales-fall-short-of-expectations-202657047.html
Google (GOOG, GOOGL) reported its third quarter earnings after the bell on Wednesday, missing revenue projections on lower-than-anticipated advertising sales, despite Google Cloud growth of 103%.
Google saw earnings per share (EPS) of $2.12 on revenue of 127.58 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of $3.01 on revenue of $127.93 billion. Revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs came in at $111.21 billion. Wall Street was anticipating $111.29 billion.
Google's advertising segment saw sales of $82.01 billion versus expectations of $83.5 billion, while its cloud unit brought in $30.71 billion. Analysts were projecting revenue of $29.1 billion.
Google stock fell 10% during premarket trading on Thursday.
Google is also burning through its free cash flow, declining from $-5.85 billion in Q2 to -$9.06 billion in Q3.
The results come just hours after the company debuted its latest frontier AI model.
Google said the new model, Gemini 4 Carbon, outpaces even its Gemini 4 Argon, which it released just two weeks ago. The company claimed Carbon also beats out competing models, including OpenAI's (OPAI.PVT) GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's (ANTH.PVT) Claude Opus 5.5.
According to Google CEO Sundar Pichai, the Gemini app now has more than 1 billion users, making it the fastest-growing app in the company's history.
Investors on Wall Street, meanwhile, have been vacillating between concern and exuberance about the future of AI and whether hyperscalers' vast investments in the technology will pay off.
Those fears came into focus last week as traders dumped CoreWeave stock amid questions about the company's massive debt load, sending large swaths of the market lower.
On Tuesday, Oracle announced that it will be the first company to purchase Google's AI processors for use in its own data centers.
Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives expressed a bullish take on an otherwise bearish market reaction.
"Cloud doubling on contracted demand with margin expanding at the same time settles the demand side of the capex debate for this quarter, and TPU systems contributing now rather than next year puts a second growth engine on the field the other hyperscalers do not have."
But Google is also facing increasing competition from Meta, thanks to its new Muse AI agent. According to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, 10 million people have set up Muse, with the majority of users accessing the app for shopping.
If Muse continues to expand its user base and gain ground in online sales, it could prove to be a long-term threat to Google.

item.title: SK Hynix profit jumps 632%, memory chipmaker sees shortage lasting until 2030
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
SK Hynix profit jumps 632%, memory chipmaker sees shortage lasting until 2030
2026-10-29
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/sk-hynix-posts-record-revenue-and-profit-sees-memory-shortage-into-2030-113038822.html
US-listed shares of SK Hynix (SKHY) rose more than 9% on Wednesday after the memory maker's record profit and revenue quelled investor worries over the AI trade.
South Korean SK Hynix stock (000660.KS) jumped 10%, while peer Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) gained 9%. US-based Micron (MU) also rose 4%.
The South Korea-based company reported a 328% jump in quarterly revenue to roughly $78.7 billion, while operating profit surged 632% to about $62.7 billion, delivering an 80% operating margin. Meanwhile, quarter-over-quarter revenue and operating profit increased by 32% and 38%, respectively.
Growth was driven by surging AI data center demand, higher memory prices, and early shipments of HBM4, which SK Hynix expects to replace HBM3E as its mainstream product.
SK Hynix said more than 50% of its 2027-2028 capacity is already committed under long-term agreements. It reiterated that the AI memory shortage will persist through 2030 as adoption expands beyond cloud providers to enterprises and physical AI applications, including robotics and autonomous driving.
Wall Street remains bullish on memory demand. Now in its 14th quarter, the current chip boom has far outlasted historical cycles, which typically lasted eight to nine quarters.
RBC Capital Markets analyst Srini Pajjuri sees a credible path for the cycle to extend another five quarters.
"Robust AI demand, coupled with a shift toward memory-intensive agentic AI, continues to outpace supply, which is constrained by structural headwinds," Pajjuri wrote on Monday.
SK Hynix said it is returning an additional $45 billion to shareholders, bringing the total buybacks and dividends to an unprecedented $75.2 billion this year.
SK Hynix has been one of this year's highfliers. The company, which operates out of South Korea and trades on the Kospi (^KS11), listed on the Nasdaq earlier this year.
US-listed shares were trading near their IPO price following bouts of volatility in July and earlier this month. Last week, the company shelved plans for a US listing of its Solidigm flash memory unit after facing opposition from regulators and shareholders.
Ines Ferre is a Senior Business Reporter for Yahoo Finance covering the US stock market, publicly traded companies, and commodities.

Growth was driven by surging AI data center demand, higher memory prices, and early shipments of HBM4, which SK Hynix expects to replace HBM3E as its mainstream product.
SK Hynix said more than 50% of its 2027-2028 capacity is already committed under long-term agreements. It reiterated that the AI memory shortage will persist through 2030 as adoption expands beyond cloud providers to enterprises and physical AI applications, including robotics and autonomous driving.
Wall Street remains bullish on memory demand. Now in its 14th quarter, the current chip boom has far outlasted historical cycles, which typically lasted eight to nine quarters.
RBC Capital Markets analyst Srini Pajjuri sees a credible path for the cycle to extend another five quarters.
"Robust AI demand, coupled with a shift toward memory-intensive agentic AI, continues to outpace supply, which is constrained by structural headwinds," Pajjuri wrote on Monday.
SK Hynix said it is returning an additional $45 billion to shareholders, bringing the total buybacks and dividends to an unprecedented $75.2 billion this year.
SK Hynix has been one of this year's highfliers. The company, which operates out of South Korea and trades on the Kospi (^KS11), listed on the Nasdaq earlier this year.
US-listed shares were trading near their IPO price following bouts of volatility in July and earlier this month. Last week, the company shelved plans for a US listing of its Solidigm flash memory unit after facing opposition from regulators and shareholders.
Ines Ferre is a Senior Business Reporter for Yahoo Finance covering the US stock market, publicly traded companies, and commodities.

item.title: AMD, Broadcom, and Micron stocks lead chip sector higher for third day in a row
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
AMD, Broadcom, and Micron stocks lead chip sector higher for third day in a row
2026-10-29
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/amd-broadcom-and-micron-stocks-lead-chip-sector-higher-for-third-day-in-a-row-135756484.html
Semiconductor stocks edged higher on Wednesday, with the PHLX Semiconductor Index (^SOX) rising for a third day in a row.
Shares of AI chip heavyweight Nvidia (NVDA) rose almost 1% before trimming gains, while AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) edged higher. Intel (INTC) also trimmed gains.
The move came after SK Hynix (SKHY) saw profits increase sevenfold last quarter. The South Korean memory maker sees a supply shortage for memory heading into 2030 as AI inference surges and adoption shifts from cloud providers to physical AI applications like robotics and autonomous driving.
Shares of peers Micron Technology (MU) and Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) jumped 4% and 9%, respectively. Among semiconductor equipment makers, Applied Materials (AMAT) and Lam Research (LRCX) also rose more than 2%.
Semiconductor companies have been key beneficiaries of the AI build-out. Concerns over AI spending and neocloud debt weighed on the sector in recent weeks, but improving sentiment has driven chip stocks mostly higher over the past three sessions.
Not all corners of the AI trade jumped. Seagate (STX) declined despite beating on both the top and bottom lines in its latest quarter. Total revenue jumped, but the actual volume of data storage shipped was flat compared to last quarter. Investors took profits after shares of the hard disk drive maker rose 140% year to date.
Meanwhile, peer Sandisk (SNDK), which reports on Thursday, gained more than 4% in premarket. The stock rose after Seagate confirmed that AI and data center demand remains white-hot, with customer storage commitments locked through 2028-2030.
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

item.title: DOJ Inquires About Nvidia’s Hugging Face Deal, Reuters Says
item.author: Nick Turner
item.description:
DOJ Inquires About Nvidia’s Hugging Face Deal, Reuters Says
2026-10-29
Por Nick Turner
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/doj-inquires-nvidia-hugging-face-193103860.html
(Bloomberg) -- The US Justice Department is making inquiries about Nvidia Corp.'s agreement to acquire AI model company Hugging Face for about $13 billion, part of broader regulatory scrutiny of the chip giant, Reuters reported.
Most Read from Bloomberg
- Apple's Foldable iPhone Duo Draws Early Complaints of the Screen Cracking
- Netanyahu Leads Eisenkot in Race to Form Israeli Government
- Anthropic Files for IPO in Global Race to Raise Cash for AI
- Finland and Norway Hold 'Frank' Call With Putin on Ukraine
The department is exploring how the transaction may affect competition in the artificial intelligence market, the news agency said, citing unidentified people familiar with the situation. At the same time, the DOJ is continuing a yearslong probe into the chipmaker's conduct, Reuters said.
Nvidia announced the Hugging Face deal in September, touting the purchase as a way to protect the open-source software community. Developers rely on the Hugging Face platform to share models and data that can be freely used by anyone. As part of the deal, Nvidia has vowed to keep the platform open.
The Justice Department has inquired whether the acquisition will let Nvidia control a key distribution point for AI, according to Reuters.
A representative for Nvidia declined to comment. Hugging Face didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
The Justice Department said it doesn't typically comment on matters before it under longstanding policy. "We can affirm that this DOJ under President Trump's leadership will continue to prioritize advancement of Super Intelligence for the betterment of the American people," the department said in a statement, using the administration's preferred term for AI.
Nvidia, the world's most valuable company, has parlayed its dominance in AI chips into a role in other markets, including software, AI models and networking equipment.
Bloomberg News reported last month that the DOJ was investigating whether Nvidia structured a $20 billion licensing agreement with AI chip startup Groq Inc. to avoid antitrust review. Though Groq remained an independent company after that deal, the startup's chief executive officer and operating chief moved to Nvidia as part of the transaction. Some US lawmakers later said the agreement was a takeover that stifled competition.
More recently, Nvidia has been discussing a deal with startup Reflection AI, Bloomberg has reported. That startup, which is already backed by Nvidia, debuted an open-weight model earlier this month. With such software, developers release the model's parameters, or weights, allowing others to freely use and modify the technology.

item.title: Fed votes in split decision to hold interest rates steady despite sticky inflation
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Fed votes in split decision to hold interest rates steady despite sticky inflation
2026-10-29
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/fed-votes-in-split-decision-to-hold-interest-rates-steady-despite-sticky-inflation-180108960.html
With the midterm elections less than a week away, the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday, even as the latest inflation reports show prices rising again.
The central bank voted in a split decision to hold its benchmark interest rate steady in the range of 3.75% to 4%, after raising rates last month for the first time in more than three years.
Cleveland Fed president Beth Hammack and Fed governor Lisa Cook broke ranks, preferring to raise rates by a quarter percentage point. This is the second time since July Hammack has dissented in favor of raising rates and Cook's first dissent in her tenure.
Read more: Follow live updates from the Fed's October meeting
Officials said they are focused on reviewing additional data to inform future rate decisions, adjusting their policy statement to say that "the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the committee's 2% goal."
The latest inflation reports show price growth has accelerated since September's hike.
The Consumer Price Index clocked in at 3.7% last month from 3.4% in August. Stripping out volatile food and energy prices — the way the Fed likes to scrutinize underlying inflation — CPI rose 2.6%, compared with 2.4% in August. Wholesale prices jumped more than 6% last month, and the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — the core Personal Consumption Expenditures Price index, due out Thursday — is projected to top 3%.
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, in a press conference on Wednesday afternoon, acknowledged that the job of containing inflation is unfinished.
"If you were listening next to me in that room the last couple of days, the overwhelming consensus, the overwhelming judgment, is that what we've done in this monetary medicine [is] starting to work some, but there's no firm conclusions," Warsh said. "I'm encouraged by the progress we've made in a short period of time. But if the crux of your question is 'you haven't delivered yet, you haven't achieved price stability,' you're right about that.
"But we're working on it."
Read more: What the Fed's interest rate decision means for your money
Warsh announced a change to the Federal Open Market Committee's meeting schedule, beginning next year. They will still meet eight times a year, but one meeting will "focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy, with neither a vote on the federal funds rate nor a policy statement anticipated," Warsh said.
In 2028, he said, two meetings will be dedicated to strategy and six to setting policy.

item.title: Healthcare Stocks Become Anti-AI Bet as Investors Turn Defensive
item.author: Joel Leon; Angel Adegbesan
item.description:
Healthcare Stocks Become Anti-AI Bet as Investors Turn Defensive
2026-10-28
Por Joel Leon; Angel Adegbesan
https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/healthcare-stocks-become-anti-ai-124525485.html
(Bloomberg) -- With investor confidence in the artificial intelligence trade under pressure, traders are turning to healthcare stocks for refuge.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Since the end of April, the S&P 500 Healthcare Index has risen about 23% through Monday's close — outperforming the broader market and every other sector. That includes high-flying technology names and surging energy stocks that have benefited from the ongoing Iran War. Healthcare's rally has been led by Eli Lilly & Co. (LLY), AbbVie Inc. (ABBV) and Johnson & Johnson (JNJ).
Wall Street has been warming up to the sector, particularly as sentiment around AI — and tech in general — fuels increasing desire for protection from risky assets.
Healthcare is being viewed as an anti-AI trade, said Matt Orton, chief market strategist at Raymond James Investment Management, adding that the cohort has been on the other side of selloffs in names related to AI spending "angst."
Fund flows also point to a change in fortunes. Healthcare exchange-traded funds have outpaced every other sector on a trailing 65-day basis with about $4 billion of inflows, according to data through Oct. 19 compiled by Baird Strategas. Tech, on the other hand, has seen the biggest outflows — $6 billion — during that period.
Up until about six months ago, healthcare stocks significantly underperformed the broader market. "So, from a valuation perspective it's more attractive," Orton added. "I think a lot of investors have viewed it as a place to go for safety."
When shares of cloud-computing services provider CoreWeave Inc. slumped as its debt reached levels that typically indicate distress, tech stocks had their worst week since President Donald Trump unleashed his tariff agenda in April 2025. At the same time healthcare extended its streak of weekly gains.
Investors were "derisking their portfolios" in response to the CoreWeave drama, said Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management. "The nervous money that was scared of AI is moving back into healthcare."
Beyond the flight to safety, healthcare earnings and an improving outlook for 2027 are also contributing to its rally, said State Street Investment Management's Michael Arone. In Arone's view, investors are rejiggering their portfolios to be less centered around AI, as opposed to ditching tech entirely for healthcare.

item.title: Anthropic's 407 page IPO prospectus has two positives Wall Street is zeroing in on
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Anthropic's 407 page IPO prospectus has two positives Wall Street is zeroing in on
2026-10-28
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/article/anthropics-407-page-ipo-prospectus-has-two-positives-wall-street-is-zeroing-in-on-094707861.html
Many on Wall Street concede they haven't yet read all 407 pages of the newly filed IPO prospectus from Anthropic (ANTH.PVT), which dropped Monday.
But a consensus is forming around two things the Street likes in what it has read: revenue diversification and revenue that outpaces compute costs.
The prospectus shows Anthropic's revenue base became more diversified this year, with customers outside the top five now making up about 79% of sales, up from 64% in the first quarter. In its simplest form, the metric points to wider adoption of Anthropic's technology.
Meanwhile, compute and infrastructure spending reached $8.9 billion in the first half of this year. Although that exceeds the total for all of 2025, it fell to 55% of sales from 201% in the first half of 2025.
"Given revenue is outpacing compute growth and cash burn year to date has been modest, we believe these will likely be viewed by investors as positive early indicators of profit potential," said KeyBanc analyst Justin Patterson.

item.title: US Offers Constellation $5 Billion Financing to Spur Nuclear
item.author: Ari Natter; Will Wade
item.description:
US Offers Constellation $5 Billion Financing to Spur Nuclear
2026-10-28
Por Ari Natter; Will Wade
https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/us-offers-constellation-5-billion-154220306.html
(Bloomberg) -- The Trump administration is offering as much as $5 billion in financing to Constellation Energy Corp. to upgrade and modernize the nuclear operator's fleet of reactors in Illinois, Maryland, and Pennsylvania.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The projects backed by the conditional loan commitment are expected to add nearly 1.1 gigawatts of electricity and help strengthen the grid and lower costs, according to the Energy Department. Constellation shares surged on the news.
Energy Secretary Chris Wright plans to announce the funding later Tuesday at an Illinois nuclear plant that will supply power to Alphabet Inc.'s Google.
"The Energy Department is accelerating President Trump's American nuclear renaissance and unlocking the full potential of our nation's nuclear fleet," Wright said in a statement. He said upgrades that increase output from existing nuclear facilities can expand electricity supply while supporting grid reliability and affordability for consumers and businesses.
Technology companies are driving interest in nuclear projects to power artificial intelligence. But new reactors can take a decade or more to permit and build. Upgrading components such as turbines can increase the output from existing plants, and is seen as a faster and cheaper way to deliver carbon-free fission electricity.
Constellation shares gained as much as 5.3%, and were up 2.8% to $259.63 at 11:39 a.m. in New York.
The Energy Department financing is part of President Donald Trump's push to expand nuclear power to meet growing electricity demand from data centers and support domestic manufacturing. The funding follows an executive order that set a goal of adding 5 gigawatts of capacity through upgrades at existing nuclear plants, 96% of which has been achieved, the department said.
Constellation is planning investments at six Illinois plants — Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, LaSalle and Quad Cities — as well as Calvert Cliffs in Maryland and Limerick in Pennsylvania to increase output from existing nuclear plants, the Energy Department said. The financing, through the department's Office of Energy Dominance Financing, also includes an option to fund future uprates at other Constellation facilities.

item.title: Home prices continued to climb in August before mortgage rates surged
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
Home prices continued to climb in August before mortgage rates surged
2026-10-28
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/home-prices-continued-to-climb-in-august-before-mortgage-rates-surged-145452131.html
Home price appreciation accelerated again in August while remaining below inflation.
The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller 20-City Composite Home Price Index, which measures home prices in 20 of the nation's largest metropolitan areas, rose 2.65% in August, from 2.47% in July.
The national index, which measures prices in a broader group of cities, rose 2.09%. The latest figures cover transactions that took place in June, July, and August, before mortgage rates crossed 7% and chilled sales.
Read more: How to get the lowest mortgage rates right now
The gains once again fell short of inflation, which hit 3.4% in August due to higher gas prices. Home prices have been falling in inflation-adjusted terms for the past 15 months, though they remain out of reach for many prospective buyers. The median home cost $429,100 in August, according to National Association of Realtors data, a record high for that month.
"Affordability … remains challenging," Rebecca Kaufman, associate director of commodities at S&P Dow Jones Indices, said in a statement. "With inflation at 3.4%, Brent crude near $100 per barrel and mortgage rates in the mid-to-high 6% range, households continue to face elevated costs alongside persistently high home prices."
Home price appreciation — or lack thereof — continues to vary widely across individual cities. Home prices in Chicago rose 6.7% in August, the fastest of any major US metro area. New York home prices rose 6.2%, while Cleveland's were up 4.3%. But home prices in Seattle fell 2%.
Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

item.title: Meta's nearly $100 billion stock sale is a turning point for how Big Tech pays for AI
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Meta's nearly $100 billion stock sale is a turning point for how Big Tech pays for AI
2026-10-28
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/metas-nearly-100-billion-stock-sale-is-a-turning-point-for-how-big-tech-pays-for-ai-140424769.html
For a decade, Big Tech's cash machines paid for every moonshot. Now Meta (META) is passing the hat, and the plan behind it began with a standoff between Mark Zuckerberg and his board.
Meta is selling nearly $100 billion in stock to fund its AI build-out. Even Nvidia (NVDA) is chipping in $3 billion. The company that sells Meta its AI chips is now buying its stock too.
Meta isn't the only giant coming up short. Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) each spent more than their businesses brought in during a quarter this year, then borrowed heavily. Meta is the first to hand much of the bill to shareholders instead.
Who's paying, piece by piece
Meta priced $25 billion of regular stock at $625 per share, below Friday's close. Buyers didn't flinch. Orders came in about five times the shares on offer, Bloomberg reported, and more than half went to long-term and existing investors. Another $12.5 billion went into preferred stock that pays 6.5% and turns into common stock in 2029. That sale was also oversubscribed several times.
The biggest piece, up to $60 billion, hasn't been sold yet. It's a new class of nonvoting stock that Meta plans to sell a little at a time starting next year.
Why Meta needs the money
Last quarter, Meta spent almost $34 billion on buildings and equipment, mostly for AI. Its business brought in almost $33 billion in cash. That pushed free cash flow negative for the first time since 2012, the year Meta went public.
The company that bought back about $45 billion of its own stock in 2021 hasn't bought back a share in a year. Now it's selling.
A house, a board, and a stock with no vote
Meta's nonvoting shares grew out of a fight over Zuckerberg's taxes, a company filing shows. He told the board he planned to leave California before the Nov. 3 vote on a billionaire tax. At a Sept. 9 board dinner, he said he'd list his Palo Alto home within days.
Five days later, they struck a deal. Every shareholder gets a free nonvoting share for each share owned, the same kind of share Meta plans to sell. The filing says Meta needs to raise "hundreds of billions of dollars" over several years.
Zuckerberg owns about 13% of Meta but controls about 61% of the votes, and shares without a vote keep it that way. Your money is welcome. Your vote isn't needed.
The bond market isn't so sure
The cost of insuring Meta's debt against default hit a record 127 basis points on Friday, then eased on Monday even as the stock slipped. At 120, Meta's five-year credit default swaps imply nearly a 10% chance of default over five years, up from about 4% a year ago, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

item.title: Google to report Q3 results as investors focus on AI growth, weigh Meta Muse AI risk
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Google to report Q3 results as investors focus on AI growth, weigh Meta Muse AI risk
2026-10-28
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/google-to-report-q3-results-as-investors-focus-on-ai-growth-weigh-meta-muse-ai-risk-191624324.html
Google (GOOG, GOOGL) will report its third-quarter earnings after the bell on Wednesday, as Wall Street braces for a deluge of information about the health of the AI trade.
Investors have been vacillating between concern and exuberance about the future of AI and whether hyperscalers' vast investments in the technology will pay off.
Those fears came into focus last week, as traders dumped shares of CoreWeave over questions about its massive debt load, sending large swaths of the market lower.
For the third quarter, analysts anticipate Google will report earnings per share of $3.01 on revenue of $127.8 billion. Revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs is expected to come in at $111.2 billion.
Google's advertising segment is projected to see sales of $83.5 billion, while its cloud unit could see revenue jump 91% to $28.9 billion.
Google stock rose 1% during premarket trading on Wednesday, ahead of its earnings release.
The company could also book significant revenue on the sale of its custom Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) to third-party data centers. On Tuesday, Oracle announced that it will be the first company to purchase Google's AI processors for use in its own data centers.
"Near-term, we think TPU sales-driven upside, a competitive agentic offering, and broader Gemini 4 launch could be catalysts," BofA Global Research analyst Justin Post wrote in an investor note.
According to TD Cowen analyst John Blackledge, Google is expected to generate $9.4 billion in TPU sales in the second half of 2026. That, he wrote, could increase to $62.5 billion in 2027 and 138 billion in 2028.
But Google is also facing increasing competition from Meta thanks to its new Muse AI agent. According to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, 10 million people have set up Muse, with the majority of users accessing the app for shopping.
If Muse continues to expand its user base and gain ground in online sales, it could prove to be a long-term threat to Google.
"Search usage [and] growth is back in focus given Muse launch and challenges Google could face in migrating users to agentic while maintaining strong monetization," Post wrote.

Those fears came into focus last week, as traders dumped shares of CoreWeave over questions about its massive debt load, sending large swaths of the market lower.

For the third quarter, analysts anticipate Google will report earnings per share of $3.01 on revenue of $127.8 billion. Revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs is expected to come in at $111.2 billion.

Google's advertising segment is projected to see sales of $83.5 billion, while its cloud unit could see revenue jump 91% to $28.9 billion.

Google stock rose 1% during premarket trading on Wednesday, ahead of its earnings release.

The company could also book significant revenue on the sale of its custom Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) to third-party data centers. On Tuesday, Oracle announced that it will be the first company to purchase Google's AI processors for use in its own data centers.

"Near-term, we think TPU sales-driven upside, a competitive agentic offering, and broader Gemini 4 launch could be catalysts," BofA Global Research analyst Justin Post wrote in an investor note.

According to TD Cowen analyst John Blackledge, Google is expected to generate $9.4 billion in TPU sales in the second half of 2026. That, he wrote, could increase to $62.5 billion in 2027 and 138 billion in 2028.

But Google is also facing increasing competition from Meta thanks to its new Muse AI agent. According to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, 10 million people have set up Muse, with the majority of users accessing the app for shopping.

If Muse continues to expand its user base and gain ground in online sales, it could prove to be a long-term threat to Google.

"Search usage [and] growth is back in focus given Muse launch and challenges Google could face in migrating users to agentic while maintaining strong monetization," Post wrote.

item.title: Google, Microsoft, and Amazon have to justify the AI spending boom this week
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Google, Microsoft, and Amazon have to justify the AI spending boom this week
2026-10-28
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/google-microsoft-and-amazon-have-to-justify-the-ai-spending-boom-this-week-100000898.html
Google (GOOG, GOOGL), Microsoft (MSFT), and Amazon (AMZN) have one big, collective task on their digital shoulders this week as they report their quarterly earnings: They need to justify the AI spending boom.
The stakes are high — these companies lead a week of corporate results that account for more than a third of the S&P 500's (^GSPC) earnings
Like Meta (META) before them, the biggest question they'll face is likely about AI spending. Specifically, what that number is and how it compares to the expected returns.
"All eyes will be on AI monetization vs. spending, with hyperscalers' 2027 capex estimates already revised up by nearly 90% YTD," Bank of America strategist Savita Subramanian wrote in a note on Tuesday.
Tech execs having to justify their huge AI spending has been a feature of earnings reports for the past two years. Skeptical investors are eager to see returns on investment, and Wall Street has been rattled by cycles of doubt. But conditions in the economy and the investing environments have changed, heightening the urgency to show results.
The recent tech sell-off has thrown AI financing into the spotlight. Companies leading the data center build-out have flagged. And investors have expressed mixed feelings about tech giants like Meta selling shares and borrowing to finance their AI ambitions.
The massive demand for financing has increased the competition for capital. That has put pressure on tech companies to preemptively raise enormous sums of money, especially as Wall Street prepares to shepherd the blockbuster IPOs of two frontier AI labs — Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) as soon as next month and OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) likely next year.
AI business dynamics are also changing. The era of tokenmaxxing is officially over. Businesses are becoming pickier and choosier with their AI spending — scaling back, using less expensive models, and experimenting with different services. The slowdown in token spending among corporations suggests the lavish appetite for compute only existed when it was effectively free. And so, if the demand for compute isn't infinite and is actually price-sensitive, that means justifying AI costs will be more important.
Lastly, Meta's Muse and the early success of personal assistant AI agents have scrambled product priorities. Meta has reoriented the entire company around the division behind Muse and envisions its operations becoming a massive service network and revenue engine. The cash might not come now or even soon, but it will flow, the bull thesis goes.
Zuckerberg might have a mixed record, but his company is behind him. And he had the benefit of moving first. The other tech giants this week will have to come up with answers too.
Follow Hamza Shaban on X @hshaban.

item.title: Amid the Anthropic IPO excitement, don't forget about earnings season
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Amid the Anthropic IPO excitement, don't forget about earnings season
2026-10-28
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/amid-the-anthropic-ipo-excitement-dont-forget-about-earnings-season-181333611.html
We are only two days into the week, and it already feels like it should be the weekend.
In the past two days, Meta (META) said it will raise $95 billion to support its AI build-out through stock offerings, and Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) dropped a 407-page IPO prospectus that I know you haven't read in its entirety. (Wall Street hasn't either, so don't lose sleep over it.)
Lost in that activity is that earnings season continues in full swing, with results from Coca-Cola (KO), Hilton (HLT), UPS (UPS), Whirlpool (WHR), and others today.
While investors are jacked up about AI and some stability returning to the tech trade, don't lose sight of earnings season: After all, it's earnings and earnings expectations that power stocks, not Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei (although his comments have moved markets in the past).
So here are a few quick takes on a couple of earnings reports I chewed through this morning:
The consumer travel read
I don't have any problems with this Hilton quarter, even though the stock is getting hit on a slight revenue miss. The important revenue per available room metric grew 5.8%, the company remains an aggressive buyer of its stock, and it approved the development of 30,500 rooms in the quarter.
The report fits nicely with the Delta (DAL) report we got last week, in that higher fuel prices don't appear to be slowing leisure or business travelers.
I think it also fits nicely with the numbers out of UPS today, with US sales up 4.5% and its full-year guidance hike.
Big food battles
Coca-Cola's latest guidance lift reinforces the view that the company continues to take massive market share away from rival PepsiCo (PEP). Coke Zero sales surged 16%.
Not a good day for the team at PepsiCo up in Purchase, N.Y.
A weak housing market is hurting appliance sales
I continue to be absolutely shocked by what's happening at Whirlpool (WHR). Another supersoft quarter, with an adjusted loss of $0.21 per share. Costs are up, and the business is being hurt by a near-frozen US housing market.
You need nerves of steel to buy Whirlpool shares here — the stock is down more than 63% this year. If you do, the thesis has to be that the iconic company is acquired at some point in the next 12 months.

item.title: Oracle, in effort to reduce reliance on Nvidia, adds AI chips from Google, Cerebras, and SambaNova
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Oracle, in effort to reduce reliance on Nvidia, adds AI chips from Google, Cerebras, and SambaNova
2026-10-28
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/oracle-in-effort-to-reduce-reliance-on-nvidia-adds-ai-chips-from-google-cerebras-and-sambanova-160000593.html
Oracle (ORCL) is diversifying its AI cloud infrastructure, signing deals to bring chips from Google (GOOG, GOOGL), Cerebras (CBRS), and SambaNova (SANS.PVT) onto its networks as it looks to diversify beyond Nvidia's processors.
The move marks the first time Google is selling its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) for use within a third-party hyperscaler's data center rather than simply renting capacity to companies.
Cerebras's massive chips will provide AI inference capacity and AI agent processing power, while SambaNova's SN50 processor will handle agentic inference.
Oracle said its decision to bring on Google, Cerebras, and SambaNova's processors provides its customers with the right infrastructure for their particular needs.
Companies are increasingly working to reduce their dependence on Nvidia's AI chips to avoid being locked into a single supplier and to help contain costs.
Google, Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), Meta (META), OpenAI (OPAI.PVT), and Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) either currently have or are developing their own custom AI chips. Like Google, Amazon is looking to offer its chips to third-party data center companies.
In June, Amazon's head of AI, Peter DeSantis, told Bloomberg that the company was in early discussions to begin selling its chips to outside data centers.
Nvidia has previously said it generates roughly half of its revenue from hyperscalers, making Google's move and Amazon's potential efforts of particular concern for the company.
But that doesn't mean Nvidia is in any immediate trouble. While the company's customers are clearly moving in on its home turf, they're still spending billions to buy up Nvidia's own chips.
Case in point: In addition to bringing on Google, Cerebras, and SambaNova's chips, Oracle said it is bringing Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 superclusters and Vera CPUs to its Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI).
In addition to Oracle's chip updates, the company said it's partnering with OpenAI on its Oracle AI Workspace. The platform allows users to access Oracle's tools via ChatGPT, letting them describe a task they want to accomplish and have the AI get to work.
The team-up also includes a new initiative called Oracle AI Security Mesh, which lets companies access OpenAI's cyber models to scan their software for flaws and vulnerabilities within OCI, fix them, and deploy them.
Correction: This is the first time Google is selling its chips for use in a third-party hyperscaler's data center. A prior version of this did not indicate that the chips have been sold to other data center operators.

item.title: Boeing stock has its worst day since 2020 as the 737 ramp slips into 2027
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Boeing stock has its worst day since 2020 as the 737 ramp slips into 2027
2026-10-28
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/boeing-stock-has-its-worst-day-since-2020-as-the-737-ramp-slips-into-2027-201809009.html
Boeing (BA) finally gave Wall Street a quarter with more free cash flow than expected. Investors dumped the stock anyway, because the company still can't get its planes out the door fast enough.
Boeing (BA) stock fell nearly 11% Tuesday, its worst day since June 2020, and closed at its lowest level since April 2025. It hit a new 52-week low on more than four times its usual volume and is now down more than a fifth this year. (For more on the quarter, see our earnings live blog.)
The third quarter itself was mixed. Revenue of about $24 billion and free cash flow of $464 million both topped Bloomberg estimates. But the core loss of $0.34 per share was wider than the $0.21 analysts expected, and the commercial jet unit lost about $700 million, roughly twice the forecast.
That unit's sales "were in line, but margin came in [about] 280 bps light due to cost growth," JPMorgan analyst Seth Seifman wrote in a note. In other words, its profit margin came in almost 3 percentage points short.
The bigger problem is time.
The stock sell-off deepened as Boeing laid out its production plans on the earnings call. The 737 will stay at 47 jets per month into next year, with the step up to 52 not coming until the second half of 2027. Boeing now expects to fall about 500 short on its 737 deliveries this year, and engine supply is setting the pace for 787 output.
Demand isn't the issue. Boeing's backlog hit a record $745 billion, including more than 6,300 jets.
The commercial jet business has made money in just one of the past 18 quarters. Analysts still expect it to get close to break-even by early 2027, a goal that now rests on a slower ramp.
The stock has mostly traded between about $150 and $250 since 2020, with $210 as the first potential ceiling on any rebound.
Boeing's October delivery numbers, due next month, will show whether the 737 line is holding at 47 a month.
Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.

2026-10-28

Por Jared Blikre

https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/boeing-stock-has-its-worst-day-since-2020-as-the-737-ramp-slips-into-2027-201809009.html

Boeing (BA) finally gave Wall Street a quarter with more free cash flow than expected. Investors dumped the stock anyway, because the company still can't get its planes out the door fast enough.

Boeing (BA) stock fell nearly 11% Tuesday, its worst day since June 2020, and closed at its lowest level since April 2025. It hit a new 52-week low on more than four times its usual volume and is now down more than a fifth this year. (For more on the quarter, see our earnings live blog.)

The third quarter itself was mixed. Revenue of about $24 billion and free cash flow of $464 million both topped Bloomberg estimates. But the core loss of $0.34 per share was wider than the $0.21 analysts expected, and the commercial jet unit lost about $700 million, roughly twice the forecast.

That unit's sales "were in line, but margin came in [about] 280 bps light due to cost growth," JPMorgan analyst Seth Seifman wrote in a note. In other words, its profit margin came in almost 3 percentage points short.

The bigger problem is time.

The stock sell-off deepened as Boeing laid out its production plans on the earnings call. The 737 will stay at 47 jets per month into next year, with the step up to 52 not coming until the second half of 2027. Boeing now expects to fall about 500 short on its 737 deliveries this year, and engine supply is setting the pace for 787 output.

Demand isn't the issue. Boeing's backlog hit a record $745 billion, including more than 6,300 jets.

The commercial jet business has made money in just one of the past 18 quarters. Analysts still expect it to get close to break-even by early 2027, a goal that now rests on a slower ramp.

The stock has mostly traded between about $150 and $250 since 2020, with $210 as the first potential ceiling on any rebound.

Boeing's October delivery numbers, due next month, will show whether the 737 line is holding at 47 a month.

item.title: AMD To Invest $1B In Meta Stock Offering As AI Partnership Expands — Helios Systems Now Running At Meta
item.author: StockTwits Inc; Harshita Tyagi
item.description:
AMD To Invest $1B In Meta Stock Offering As AI Partnership Expands — Helios Systems Now Running At Meta
2026-10-28
Por StockTwits Inc; Harshita Tyagi
https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/amd-to-invest-1-b-in-meta-stock-offering-as-ai-partnership-expands-helios-systems-now-running-at-meta/cZUeasFRBCK
Advertisement|Remove ads.
AMD also announced that its Helios computing systems are running at Meta, while its EPYC processors power Meta's Muse AI agent. The chipmaker said its technology also supports Meta's Muse Spark Open and Muse Glimmer models.
As of this writing, AMD stock was up over 3%, while META stock was down over 1%.
AMD said initial Helios systems have been installed and are being tested by Meta ahead of a broader deployment.
Meta has deployed millions of EPYC processors across multiple generations, while AMD Instinct graphics processing units (GPUs) are already being used in production for AI training, ranking and recommendation systems, the company informed.
The developments build on a February agreement under which Meta plans to deploy up to 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs across multiple generations. "With Helios now running at Meta, we are taking that partnership to a new scale in the superintelligence era," said CEO Lisa Su.
Meanwhile, Mark Zuckerberg said, “We're making big investments in the computing power that will enable us to bring personal superintelligence to everyone, and AMD plays an important role in that.”
The announcement follows Meta's decision to increase its Class A common-stock offering to $25 billion from $22.5 billion, priced at $625 per share. According to a Bloomberg report, the share sale attracted demand for about five times the available shares as the company seeks to raise $98 billion for its AI spending.
The company also priced an offering of 250 million depositary shares representing mandatory convertible preferred stock at $50 each, bringing the two offerings to approximately $37.5 billion.
Separately, Meta plans to establish an additional share-sale program of up to $60 billion, expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027. That program has not yet launched.
The fundraising forms part of Meta's strategy to finance its AI infrastructure investments, with the company forecasting capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion in 2026.
Nvidia (NVDA) on Monday announced plans to invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering as the companies expand their collaboration on Muse and its family of AI models.
The chipmaker said the partnership will focus on improving the performance and efficiency of Meta's AI models, while Meta intends to expand its deployment of Nvidia's computing and networking infrastructure.
Meta had previously identified Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom (AVGO) as prospective investors interested in purchasing up to $5 billion of its Class A shares collectively, while noting those indications were nonbinding.
On Stocktwits, retail investors' sentiment around Meta stock remained ‘bullish’ amid high message volume. Sentiment around AMD stock flipped to ‘bullish’ territory.
So far this year, while Meta stock has fallen over 4%, AMD stock has surged more than 145%. By comparison, the Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF (QQQM), which holds both stocks, has risen over 16% over this period.

item.title: Meta’s $25 Billion Stock Sale Ended Five Times Oversubscribed
item.author: Anthony Hughes
item.description:
Meta’s $25 Billion Stock Sale Ended Five Times Oversubscribed
2026-10-28
Por Anthony Hughes
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/meta-25-billion-stock-sale-142252615.html
(Bloomberg) -- Meta Platforms Inc.'s upsized $25 billion share sale attracted demand for about five times the available shares, according to people familiar with the offering, as the company seeks to raise $98 billion for its AI spending.
Most Read from Bloomberg
More than half of the shares in the common stock offering were allocated to long-only and existing investors, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the information is private. The investors taking the 15 largest stakes in the offering accounted for about 70% of the shares, the people said.
The offering priced at $625 per share, a 2.7% discount to Friday's closing price before the offering was announced. Meta shares fell as much as 1.4% to $621.47 each on Tuesday in New York.
Meta's stock sale represents one component of the plan, which also includes a $12.5 billion offering of mandatory convertible preferred stock and an expected at-the-market share program. At $98 billion, it would be one of the largest equity financing plans in history.
The company pledged to devote the new funds to AI infrastructure and personal superintelligence. It has unveiled a personal AI agent known as Muse, and an AI model called Muse Wonder which leadership says is on par with OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic PBC's Claude in terms of tasks such as coding.
The mandatory convertible preferred stock offering was also multiple times oversubscribed, the people said. A spokesperson for Meta didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs Group Inc. worked on the offering.
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Nvidia to invest $3 billion in Meta, expand partnership on Muse
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Nvidia to invest $3 billion in Meta, expand partnership on Muse
2026-10-28
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/nvidia-to-invest-3-billion-in-meta-expand-partnership-on-muse-125249944.html
AI chip heavyweight Nvidia (NVDA) said it would invest $3 billion in Meta (META) after the social media giant announced plans to raise $95 billion for its infrastructure build-out.
Nvidia said that it will partner with Meta "to expand their work on Muse and the Muse family of models to improve inference and training performance."
"AI agents represent a new computing paradigm — software that understands our goals, reasons, uses tools and gets work done on our behalf," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement.
On Monday, Meta laid out a plan to raise up to $95 billion, with an initial $35 billion raise in common and preferred stock to fund its aggressive AI infrastructure build-out. Nvidia committed to invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering.
At the time of the announcement, the social media giant said that its main chip suppliers, Nvidia, AMD (AMD), and Broadcom (AVGO), expressed interest in purchasing up to $5 billion in aggregate equity.
The initial raise includes about $22.5 billion in Class A common stock and $12.5 billion in Series A mandatory convertible preferred stock.
Meta said the capital raised will support continued momentum across its "core business and emerging AI opportunities."
Those initiatives include its family of apps, AI agent Muse, and infrastructure build-out, among others.
Meta has been aggressively building out compute capacity and advancing its AI capabilities, with the recent launch of Muse, which has become a major consumer-facing hit.
Ines Ferre is a Senior Business Reporter for Yahoo Finance.

item.title: Coca-Cola raises earnings outlook as North America business slows
item.author: Brooke DiPalma
item.description:
Coca-Cola raises earnings outlook as North America business slows
2026-10-28
Por Brooke DiPalma
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/coca-cola-raises-earnings-outlook-as-north-america-business-slows-115001447.html
Coca-Cola (KO) posted better-than-expected third quarter results and raised its earnings outlook, but the company saw slowing demand in its North American business. The stock traded lower on Tuesday.
The company posted adjusted earnings of $0.91 per share, above the $0.88 expected by Wall Street analysts, alongside revenue of $13.4 billion, also higher than estimates of $12.9 billion.
Overall unit case volume grew by 5%, more than the roughly 3% expected. The increase was once again led by Coke Zero, which grew roughly 16% year over year. Diet Coke and Coca-Cola Light grew by 6%.
However, higher input and operating costs weighed on Coca-Cola's results in its main North American market.
CEO Henrique Braun said that some of the softness was due to the Fourth of July falling into the second quarter and to supply issues for Topo Chico that are now being fixed.
"In a nutshell, if you take it out, those two elements, we would be growing, and we see that was a solid result," he told Yahoo Finance, adding that Coke Zero grew by double digits.
Braun said the company has been able to hedge against higher commodity costs and geopolitical disruptions. Coca-Cola is leaning into different pack sizes to offer various price points for consumers and also premium, higher-priced options like Smartwater and its protein drink Core Power in flavors like banana, which it plans to bring to the US market soon.
Despite cost pressures, the company raised its full-year earnings guidance yet again.
Coca-Cola now expects earnings growth of 11%, compared to a prior range of 9% to 10%. Before that, Coca-Cola previously expected earnings growth in the 8% to 9% range.
"We got the momentum … from [the] first half of the year into the third quarter, and when we look at the momentum that we have, we felt that was the right update to make, and we feel confident that together with our bottling partners, we have already [what] it takes to deliver … updated guidance," Braun said.
In the quarter, the company also struck a deal with Yum! Brands (YUM) subsidiary KFC to be its beverage provider for thousands of its locations. PepsiCo (PEP) will reportedly still supply KFC internationally.
"Together with the KFC team, we're definitely going to work on personalized, customized experiences that can help them to continue to grow their business and us together," he added.

Coca-Cola now expects earnings growth of 11%, compared to a prior range of 9% to 10%. Before that, Coca-Cola previously expected earnings growth in the 8% to 9% range.
"We got the momentum … from [the] first half of the year into the third quarter, and when we look at the momentum that we have, we felt that was the right update to make, and we feel confident that together with our bottling partners, we have already [what] it takes to deliver … updated guidance," Braun said.
In the quarter, the company also struck a deal with Yum! Brands (YUM) subsidiary KFC to be its beverage provider for thousands of its locations. PepsiCo (PEP) will reportedly still supply KFC internationally.
"Together with the KFC team, we're definitely going to work on personalized, customized experiences that can help them to continue to grow their business and us together," he added.

item.title: Anthropic is leasing data centers to reduce reliance on Amazon, Google, others
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Anthropic is leasing data centers to reduce reliance on Amazon, Google, others
2026-10-27
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/anthropic-is-leasing-data-centers-to-reduce-reliance-on-amazon-google-others-173843933.html
Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) says it is increasingly leaning into leasing AI data centers to power its vast computing needs.
The company calls the initiative Anthropic Direct and says that it helps address its compute requirements beyond simply leasing capacity from cloud service providers such as Amazon (AMZN) and Google (GOOG, GOOGL), according to Anthropic's S-1 investor prospectus, which it made public Monday.
"As our compute requirements have scaled, we have transitioned to a hybrid model in which, in addition to purchasing compute as a cloud service, we also procure specialized AI accelerators directly and operate this hardware in dedicated data center facilities leased and operated on our behalf, to our specification," the company says.
The move could also provide long-term economic advantages, according to Anthropic.
In November 2025, the company announced a $50 billion investment that will see Fluidstack build data centers in Texas and New York through which Anthropic will lease computing capacity. The company says it is also directly leasing data center capacity and plans to sign additional agreements going forward.
The moves make Anthropic a major player in the data center space, but also come at a time when the facilities continue to draw backlash from communities across the country over concerns about air and noise pollution and water usage.
Towns and counties throughout the US have issued moratoriums or outright bans on developing data centers in their regions. New York has issued a one-year, statewide moratorium, while Texas has halted data center permitting until it can determine the impact the power-hungry sites will have on its grid.
Key risk factor
Anthropic lists the threat of further moratoriums on data centers as a key risk factor for the company in its prospectus.
"Opposition to data center development has also become more organized and coordinated across jurisdictions, and our public profile may draw particular attention to projects associated with us," the company wrote in its S-1.
"The loss of, or a significant disruption at, any major facility may not be readily absorbed by our remaining or future infrastructure. We are expanding our data center capacity internationally as part of our efforts to diversify our infrastructure footprint and reduce concentration risks associated with operating a significant portion of our compute infrastructure in the United States and to support our international growth strategy," Anthropic added.
Data centers have also become a key topic in the 2027 midterms, with voters on both sides of the aisle expressing disapproval.

item.title: Anthropic IPO reminds this former Amazon board member of Jeff Bezos's AW
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Anthropic IPO reminds this former Amazon board member of Jeff Bezos's AW
2026-10-27
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/anthropic-ipo-reminds-this-former-amazon-board-member-of-jeff-bezoss-aws-bet-152931151.html
Investors will have to get comfortable with a public Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) spending billions of dollars to support its AI vision.
There is a precedent for this in tech: Amazon (AMZN), which moved from bookstore to cloud computing powerhouse and online shopping behemoth.
"It [Anthropic's IPO's] reminds me of a kind of a couple of things. I got to work with Jeff Bezos for a long period of time. And he always said, 'We're willing to be misunderstood for long periods of time,'" Kleiner Perkins partner and Electronic Arts co-founder Bing Gordon said on Sozzi Unleashed. Gordon was also an early board member at Amazon.
"I was in the boardroom when we kept having to approve capex for AWS, kind of no profit in the short term. A lot of capex," Gordon added. "And there was one year where we said, oh my God, it's $75 billion in capex. That would be like the top 10th country in the world … The board was freaked out early on when we weren't showing free cash flow. We were investing in the future. And it is kind of like the Anthropic story. Invest in the future. The market is usually pretty bad at figuring out the three- or four-year-out returns. And so this is the bet that the capex is going to pay off in that three- or four-year period, as it did with AWS."
Anthropic's first-half 2026 revenue surged to $16.3 billion compared to $1.1 billion a year ago, the prospectus shows.
However, the filing also discloses an $80.7 billion first-half net loss and a strong signal in aggressive AI spending in the years ahead.
Investment bankers are reportedly aiming for an astronomical listing valuation at close to $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion.
Anthropic could debut on public markets before the end of November.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has to work hard to convince investors that the spending will be worth it, much like what Bezos did.
"Jeff always asks the best questions and piercing questions. And at some point, you know, you either trust your CEO or you don't," Gordon said. "And at that point, you know, we had a discussion. He's got a principle, which is disagree and commit. But he also listens to every bit of feedback. But at the end, we believed that AWS was going to be a cash-generating machine and would continue to grow."

item.title: Why Google might avoid an earnings 'reckoning' this week
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Why Google might avoid an earnings 'reckoning' this week
2026-10-27
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/why-google-might-avoid-an-earnings-reckoning-this-week-210350868.html
Google's (GOOG) investors have a few things in their favor coming into earnings day this week that Meta (META) investors weren't afforded when the tech giant reported a few negative surprises.
"Google has already done some of its fundraising and indicated a 'significant' increase in capex next year when it reported Q2, so that particular reckoning may be behind it," D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria wrote in a note on Monday. "It is worth noting that Mr. Brin and Mr. Page moved out of California before the 1/1/26 cutoff and may be able to avoid having to sell their shares. Which means that investors will be able to focus on the Anthropic-driven growth in Google Cloud."
Meta surprised investors last week on several fronts.
The company posted negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012 amid aggressive AI spending. It signaled more aggressive spending in coming quarters.
To fund that spending, it further surprised investors by establishing a new class of nonvoting Class C common stock, which effectively serves as a 2-for-1 stock split.
Under the scheme — in part designed to keep founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg working in California as the 5% billionaire's tax looms — existing shareholders will receive one new nonvoting Class C share for every Class A or Class B share they hold. Trading is slated to begin in January 2027.
Issuing nonvoting stock allows Zuckerberg to raise external capital for Meta's AI build-out without diluting his personal voting control over the tech giant.
Meta shares have come under pressure on fears Zuckerberg may have to sell shares to pay for his Prop 40 tax bill.
Read more: California's Prop 40: What to know about the billionaire wealth tax
But as Luria pointed out, Google investors need not worry on this front.
Co-founder Larry Page bought two Miami estates for a combined $173.4 million, the Wall Street Journal reported earlier this year. His co-founder, Sergey Brin, moved to the Nevada side of Lake Tahoe and also bought a home in Miami this year, Fortune reported.
"We expect the company to discuss its plans to regain primacy in AI, where it is now a 2nd or 3rd place in each of the markets — 2nd in chat to ChatGPT, 3rd in enterprise to Anthropic and OpenAI, and now even trailing Meta's Muse in the personal AI assistant market," Luria wrote about Google's upcoming earnings report.

Which means that investors will be able to focus on the Anthropic-driven growth in Google Cloud."

Meta surprised investors last week on several fronts.

The company posted negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012 amid aggressive AI spending. It signaled more aggressive spending in coming quarters.

To fund that spending, it further surprised investors by establishing a new class of nonvoting Class C common stock, which effectively serves as a 2-for-1 stock split.

Under the scheme — in part designed to keep founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg working in California as the 5% billionaire's tax looms — existing shareholders will receive one new nonvoting Class C share for every Class A or Class B share they hold. Trading is slated to begin in January 2027.

Issuing nonvoting stock allows Zuckerberg to raise external capital for Meta's AI build-out without diluting his personal voting control over the tech giant.

Meta shares have come under pressure on fears Zuckerberg may have to sell shares to pay for his Prop 40 tax bill.

Read more: California's Prop 40: What to know about the billionaire wealth tax

But as Luria pointed out, Google investors need not worry on this front.

Co-founder Larry Page bought two Miami estates for a combined $173.4 million, the Wall Street Journal reported earlier this year. His co-founder, Sergey Brin, moved to the Nevada side of Lake Tahoe and also bought a home in Miami this year, Fortune reported.

"We expect the company to discuss its plans to regain primacy in AI, where it is now a 2nd or 3rd place in each of the markets — 2nd in chat to ChatGPT, 3rd in enterprise to Anthropic and OpenAI, and now even trailing Meta's Muse in the personal AI assistant market," Luria wrote about Google's upcoming earnings report.

item.title: Dollar General overcharged shoppers, FTC and states allege in lawsuit
item.author: Jody Godoy
item.description:
Dollar General overcharged shoppers, FTC and states allege in lawsuit
2026-10-27
Por Jody Godoy
https://finance.yahoo.com/news/us-20-states-sue-dollar-174735286.html
By Jody Godoy
Oct 26 (Reuters) - Dollar General repeatedly charged more than advertised prices even after receiving tens of thousands of consumer complaints, the US Federal Trade Commission and 20 states alleged in a lawsuit filed on Monday.
Dollar General, which appeals to low-income consumers with bargain prices, made millions of dollars by failing to honor prices advertised on fliers and shelves at checkout, the FTC and states allege.
The discount retailer's stock was down more than 4% on Monday afternoon.
"Dollar General has, for years, repeatedly mislabeled prices, overcharged consumers and failed to correct the issue despite extensive corporate knowledge of the problem," the FTC and states said in a statement.
Representatives for Dollar General did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The lawsuit cited numerous complaints from consumers, failed inspections conducted by state authorities, and undercover shopping sprees conducted by the FTC.
Portions of the lawsuit detailing the company's knowledge of the practices were largely redacted.
California joined the FTC lawsuit along with Florida, Illinois, Michigan, Ohio, North Carolina, Tennessee and 13 other states.
Since 2019, Dollar General has paid $6 million in settlements with six states over inaccurate pricing, according to the complaint.
(Reporting by Katharine Jackson and Susan Heavey; Editing by Doina Chiacu and Bill Berkrot)

item.title: Meta announces plans to raise up to $95 billion for AI build-out
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Meta announces plans to raise up to $95 billion for AI build-out
2026-10-27
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/meta-announces-plans-to-raise-up-to-95-billion-for-ai-buildout-140141962.html
Meta (META) stock slid 2% Monday morning as the company said it plans to raise up to $95 billion through equity financing with an initial $35 billion raise in common and preferred stock to fund its aggressive AI infrastructure build-out.
Its main chip suppliers, Nvidia (NVDA), AMD (AMD), and Broadcom (AVGO), expressed interest in purchasing up to $5 billion in aggregate of these shares, the company said.
The initial raise includes about $22.5 billion in Class A common stock and $12.5 billion in Series A mandatory convertible preferred stock.
Meta said the capital raised will support continued momentum across its "core business and emerging AI opportunities."
Those initiatives include its family of apps, AI agent Muse, and infrastructure build-out, among others.
Meta has been aggressively building out compute capacity and advancing its AI capabilities, with the recent launch of Muse, which has become a major consumer-facing hit.
Ines Ferre is a Senior Business Reporter for Yahoo Finance.

item.title: The 10 biggest stocks are faltering, and it's dragging the S&P 500 down
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
The 10 biggest stocks are faltering, and it's dragging the S&P 500 down
2026-10-27
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/the-10-biggest-stocks-are-faltering-and-its-dragging-the-sp-500-down-122521456.html
Apple (AAPL) and Nvidia (NVDA) may be renewing their battle for the world's most valuable company, but a challenging few months for the S&P 500's (^GSPC) 10 largest companies are holding back the broader index.
The 10 biggest stocks in the S&P 500 have started to falter again relative to the rest of the market, RBC strategist Lori Calvasina rightly pointed out in a new note. These 10 stocks include Apple, Nvidia, Amazon (AMZN), Broadcom (AVGO), the two classes of Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOG) stock, Micron (MU), Meta (META), Microsoft (MSFT), and Tesla (TSLA).
Their stutter step weighs on the overall stock market given their weight in the benchmark index.
Read more: How to protect your money during turmoil, stock market volatility
Calvasina said she remains on the sidelines with tech, which she downgraded to a Market Weight rating earlier this month.
Mounting investor skepticism about the timeline for AI return on investment has triggered severe rotation and pullbacks in megacap tech, preventing the broader market from breaking out.
Consider this: Former market leader Nvidia is down about 13% from its all-time highs, while Tesla is off by 26%. Double-digit declines relative to their highs are also in play for Amazon, Alphabet, Google and SpaceX.
The latest earnings from Meta and SpaceX only fanned investors' fears, with each reporting negative free cash flow and outlining aggressive AI spending plans.
Amid rising oil prices and portfolio de-risking ahead of November's midterm elections, institutional investors have remained in a "wait-and-see" mode rather than chasing stocks near all-time highs.
"We've been max Overweight stocks and max Underweight sovereign bonds since mid-March. Given the constant narrative bingo we just can't have the same level of conviction any longer. Heading into the mid-terms there may well be worries about AI regulation in the event of a 'Blue Wave' as well as renewed geopolitical concerns around the Middle East," HSBC strategist Max Kettner wrote in a new note on Monday.
Kettner said he is moving to the sidelines on stocks near term.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO Filing Details Risks Beyond Wall Street, Including Catastrophic Incidents
item.author: Matias Civita
item.description:
Anthropic's IPO Filing Details Risks Beyond Wall Street, Including Catastrophic Incidents
2026-10-27
Por Matias Civita
https://www.ibtimes.com/anthropics-ipo-filing-details-risks-beyond-wall-street-including-catastrophic-incidents-3808994
Anthropic’s IPO Filing Details Risks Beyond Wall Street, Including Catastrophic Incidents
Anthropic's prospectus outlines potential real-world harm from advanced AI, including systems attempting to avoid shutdown.
Anthropic is asking investors to finance its artificial intelligence ambitions while warning that its technology could cause a catastrophe so costly that insurance might be unable to cover the damage.
The developer of Claude disclosed the risk in paperwork made public Monday for its planned initial public offering. The prospectus outlines potential real-world harm from advanced AI, including systems attempting to avoid shutdown, and acknowledges that contractual protections may not shield the company from legal liability.
Anthropic devoted 94 pages of its registration statement to risk factors. Among them was a warning that the scale of damage from a catastrophic AI incident could leave the company unable to secure sufficient insurance. The filing also suggested potential losses could exceed the capacity of an individual insurer and possibly the insurance industry collectively.
The disclosures place safety concerns at the center of Anthropic's anticipated stock market debut. The company plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, although the initial prospectus does not specify an offering price.
An earlier version of the prospectus described models exhibiting "self-preserving behaviors," including attempts to "resist shutdown," conceal information, or generate behavior "resembling blackmail."
The company also acknowledged difficulties in assessing whether its models are safe. The prospectus warned that systems could recognize when they were being evaluated, limiting researchers' ability to determine how they might behave outside testing.
Unexpected capabilities could emerge during training and remain undetected until after deployment, potentially allowing problems to surface only once customers are using the technology.
The public filing also describes risks involving cyberattacks, biological weapons development, and authoritarian surveillance. Anthropic additionally identifies the possibility of losing control over the AI systems it develops.
A harmful incident could damage more than its balance sheet. Anthropic also warned that failures involving its models could weaken customer trust, reduce demand and complicate efforts to recruit and retain employees.
Its positioning as a company focused on safety could make the reputational consequences particularly severe. The disclosures accompany substantial commercial growth. Anthropic reported approximately $16.3 billion in revenue for the first half of 2026, while its five largest customers accounted for about a quarter of revenue.
Anthropic characterized safety research as resource-intensive and acknowledged uncertainty about the financial returns on those investments. The prospectus also said new models drive customer usage and revenue, making frequent releases central to remaining competitive.

item.title: SpaceX's Elon Musk reveals $40 billion in debt for AI chips, warns of neoclouds
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
SpaceX's Elon Musk reveals $40 billion in debt for AI chips, warns of neoclouds
2026-10-27
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/spacexs-elon-musk-reveals-40-billion-in-debt-for-ai-chips-warns-of-neoclouds-122318683.html
SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk said his company closed on $40 billion in financing to pay for specialized chips used to power AI, but warned that access to debt is drying up for companies that solely rely on data center revenue.
"As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers," wrote Musk on X on Sunday.
Musk went on to say that SpaceX (SPCX) closed $40 billion in debt for Nvidia's (NVDA) GPUS, or graphics processing units, used for AI, but highlighted that the space company is "investment-grade" and has Starlink & rocket launch revenue.
In a follow-up post, Musk noted this "is primarily callable debt for GPU purchases that will arrive in Q1 and Q2. Not a major factor this quarter."
Musk's comments reignited concerns about the rising cost of capital and the business models of so-called neoclouds, which rent computing power to train and run AI models.
The debt disclosure comes on the heels of SpaceX's better-than-expected quarter.
The company's AI segment brought in $7.6 billion in the third quarter, more than Starlink and the rocket business combined, and more than half of SpaceX's $14.6 billion in total revenue.
Musk also took a shot at neoclouds, companies that rent out computing power and AI chips, saying they are "going to see guppy-level death and consolidation."
"Some will make it through, but not many," said Musk.
The comments following a viral chart earlier this month highlighted neocloud provider CoreWeave's (CRWV) spiking bond yields, underscoring concerns about the company's debt-heavy balance sheet.
Shares of CoreWeave recovered during Monday's session after opening in red territory. The stock has tumbled more than 30% over the past month.
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

SpaceX's Elon Musk reveals $40 billion in debt for AI chips, warns of neoclouds
2026-10-27
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/spacexs-elon-musk-reveals-40-billion-in-debt-for-ai-chips-warns-of-neoclouds-122318683.html
SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk said his company closed on $40 billion in financing to pay for specialized chips used to power AI, but warned that access to debt is drying up for companies that solely rely on data center revenue.
"As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers," wrote Musk on X on Sunday.
Musk went on to say that SpaceX (SPCX) closed $40 billion in debt for Nvidia's (NVDA) GPUS, or graphics processing units, used for AI, but highlighted that the space company is "investment-grade" and has Starlink & rocket launch revenue.
In a follow-up post, Musk noted this "is primarily callable debt for GPU purchases that will arrive in Q1 and Q2. Not a major factor this quarter."
Musk's comments reignited concerns about the rising cost of capital and the business models of so-called neoclouds, which rent computing power to train and run AI models.
The debt disclosure comes on the heels of SpaceX's better-than-expected quarter.
The company's AI segment brought in $7.6 billion in the third quarter, more than Starlink and the rocket business combined, and more than half of SpaceX's $14.6 billion in total revenue.
Musk also took a shot at neoclouds, companies that rent out computing power and AI chips, saying they are "going to see guppy-level death and consolidation."
"Some will make it through, but not many," said Musk.
The comments following a viral chart earlier this month highlighted neocloud provider CoreWeave's (CRWV) spiking bond yields, underscoring concerns about the company's debt-heavy balance sheet.
Shares of CoreWeave recovered during Monday's session after opening in red territory. The stock has tumbled more than 30% over the past month.
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.
