Go to

Account

, then

Profiles

, and choose your child's profile.

Open

Viewing restrictions

. Netflix will ask for your account password.

Under

Title restrictions

, type each show's name, and select it to block it.

Save.

The blocked shows disappear from that profile, though it can take a little while to update on the TV.

A few other tips to help for now:

Lower the maturity rating.

Some creator shows aimed at older kids may disappear automatically if the profile is set to a younger rating.

Lock the other profiles.

Add a PIN to adult profiles so kids can't easily switch over.

Check back occasionally.

Netflix is adding more creator content, so a title-by-title block list may need updating.

There's No Off Switch for Digital Parenting
2026-10-25
Por Newsletter
The quiet, often exhausting work of keeping up with kids' digital lives, and how to share it.
The Parent Edit
By Jill Murphy, Common Sense Media
Edition #35 | October 23, 2026
The Second Shift That Is Digital Parenting
Feel free to read this part aloud to your partner, co-parent, or any other supporting caregiver in your family's life. ;) Seriously. As if the usual responsibilities of being an adult
and
a parent aren't enough, digital parenting comes with its own running list: Parental controls. Decisions. Updates. Dashboards. Finding the good apps. Blocking the bad content. Keeping up with the workarounds. Plus the quiet dread of constantly wondering whether you've missed something.
And that's just the devices.
This is why I'm always telling parents, "Give me a scary movie any day." A scary movie has been scripted, edited, and produced by professionals. I know what's in it. I can read a review. It's everything I
can't
preview that worries me: the posts, the comments, the texts, the things my kids come across when I'm not there, and whether those things are lodging somewhere in their mind. Sometimes I wonder what they've seen that they were too scared, too embarrassed, or simply too used to seeing to think they should tell me about it.
The Digital Mental Load is all too real.
If you're sharing the parenting, you should be sharing this part, too.
Learn the platforms. You don't need to know every feature. But know how your kids are using them, where the settings live, and enough to follow the conversation when something comes up.
Take the lead on some of the hard stuff. Own part of the setup, the monitoring, or the "no, not that app" conversations, so the person who usually handles it gets to enjoy some of the fun. We want to pick the movie and share the funny videos with the kids too!
Share the parental controls. Running this space can feel like a second job. If one person always knows the passwords, settings, rules, and latest workaround, that person is probably carrying too much of it. Split up what you can.

item.title: Netflix is losing viewers — but they're still subscribed
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Netflix is losing viewers — but they're still subscribed
2026-10-23
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/netflix-is-losing-viewers--but-theyre-still-subscribed-100000245.html
Netflix (NFLX) has a unique problem: subscription zombies.
The company is seeing sagging engagement in the US, while also claiming an industry-low churn rate. People aren't leaving the service, but they aren't watching it enthusiastically, either.
If the company's stock price — down 30% this year — is any indication, investors are fed up. But the steep fall from prior highs is, given the right insights and conviction, another buying opportunity.
That's how analysts at Deutsche Bank see things. In a note published Wednesday, Bryan Kraft made the case for buying the dip.
After the company reported third quarter earnings, Netflix stock fell to its lowest level in more than two years as the streaming giant missed estimates on the current quarter's revenue outlook and the full-year ad revenue forecast.
As management acknowledged there's room for its US business to do better, Kraft took a contrarian take.
Netflix viewing continues to grow outside the US, and in every region churn is down compared to last year, despite recent price hikes, he said.
"We found management's commentary on churn, international viewing, new content leadership, and their long-term growth outlook all pretty encouraging," he said.
The market has fixated on sagging time spent watching and a lackluster slate of content. But Kraft believes this stems from a weaker lineup compared to last year, rather than a deeper decline in quality.
Netflix's stock market struggle and its engagement problem both arrive with a dose of irony. After all, Paramount's (SKYD) stated justification for pursuing Warner Bros. was to get big enough to compete with Netflix. But Netflix is looking less like an indomitable tech giant and more like a beleaguered studio struggling to convince American audiences that it isn't a slop factory.
The recent executive shakeups also suggest that Netflix had ceded, or perhaps never really went after, the sought-after TV shows and movies that people associate with Apple TV and HBO Max.
But Kraft said that the growth outlook for Netflix remains healthy, even with some deceleration next year. There's member growth, price increases, more box office revenue, and advertising to support a more bullish thesis.

item.title: Meta's new nonvoting shares create an overhang — and Wall Street wants it gone
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Meta's new nonvoting shares create an overhang — and Wall Street wants it gone
2026-10-23
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/metas-new-nonvoting-shares-create-an-overhang--and-wall-street-wants-it-gone-124900698.html
Meta (META) has created a new overhang on its stock that Wall Street wasn't expecting when it established a new class of stock.
The Street's advice to Mark Zuckerberg and his team: Issue the stock fast so the focus can return to the clear product momentum the company is enjoying with its new Muse AI agent.
"The sooner the better in our view as it would remove the overhang and the Street now knows it will have non-voting shares in Jan'27, and Meta can still do a substantial equity raise before then without even coming close to impacting Mark's voting control," JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth said.
Meta announced late Wednesday that it is establishing a new class of nonvoting Class C common stock, which effectively serves as a 2-for-1 stock split.
Under the scheme — in part designed to keep founder Mark Zuckerberg working in California as the 5% billionaire's tax looms — existing shareholders will receive one new nonvoting Class C share for every Class A or Class B share they hold. Trading is slated to begin in January 2027.
Read more: What to know about the billionaire tax on the California ballot
Issuing nonvoting stock allows Zuckerberg to raise external capital for Meta's AI build-out without diluting his personal voting control over the tech giant.
The news took some air out of the balloon on what was an impressive quarter for Meta amid signs that its AI investments are paying off.
Meta's core advertising business reported a 26% increase in total revenue to $64.6 billion, powered by AI-driven recommendations, higher ad volume, and rising ad prices.
GAAP earnings per share came in at $3.83 versus analyst estimates of $3.56.
Meta stock fell 8% on Thursday.
"Net/net, some near-term noise in Meta shares, but we're encouraged by core Advertising and Meta's outlook for strong overall revenue growth in 2027, and the path to superintelligence is increasingly clear w/the Muse series of models & products," Anmuth said.

item.title: Chip stocks fall as equipment maker Lam Research cites 'supply chain constraints'
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Chip stocks fall as equipment maker Lam Research cites 'supply chain constraints'
2026-10-23
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/chip-stocks-fall-as-equipment-maker-lam-research-cites-supply-chain-constraints-130648719.html
Semiconductor stocks fell on Thursday as a major equipment supplier cited supply chain constraints on its earnings call.
The PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOXX) tumbled more than 6% amid investor concerns that such limitations could potentially hurt chip sales. AI chip heavyweight Nvidia (NVDA) and Qualcomm (QCOM) dropped more 42%, while Marvell (MRVL) and Intel (INTC) shares were down 9% and 7%, respectively.
Shares of chip developer Broadcom (AVGO) also fell more than 4%. Despite reaching an all-time high earlier this year, the stock is now flat year to date.
Meanwhile, memory and storage highfliers Micron Technology (MU) and Sandisk (SNDK) were also in red territory.
Shares of the wafer equipment maker Lam Research (LRCX) fell as much as 11% after CFO Doug Bettinger said the quarterly revenue guidance of $8.6 billion "would have been a bit higher if not for some near-term supply chain constraints," which the company is actively managing.
Other equipment makers Applied Materials (AMAT) and ASML (ASML) declined 7% and 6%, respectively.
Semiconductor stocks have been volatile in recent sessions as concerns over AI funding have weighed on the sector. Semiconductor companies have been a key beneficiary of the artificial intelligence build-out.
On Thursday, the overall stock market was set to open lower as oil prices surged, raising expectations that the Federal Reserve may have to keep tightening monetary policy this year.
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

item.title: P&G beats estimates as price hikes haven’t hurt demand yet
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
P&G beats estimates as price hikes haven’t hurt demand yet
2026-10-23
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/pg-beats-estimates-as-price-hikes-havent-hurt-demand-yet-111851559.html
Procter & Gamble's (PG) price hikes aren't crushing a consumer base dealing with higher inflation, yet.
The Tide maker delivered sales and profit upside for its fiscal first quarter on Thursday. The company maintained its full-year sales and profit outlooks.
"The US consumer is remarkably resilient," P&G CFO Andre Schulten told Yahoo Finance.
Schulten said the business is being powered by higher income households, while the lower end is being more cautious.
P&G shares rose 2% in pre-market trading.
P&G Earnings Analysis
- Net sales: $23.28 billion, +4% from the prior year vs. $22.82 billion estimate
- Organic sales growth: +4% vs. +1.96% estimate
- Beauty segment organic revenue growth: +5.4% vs. +3.58% estimate
- Grooming segment organic revenue growth: +4.5% vs. +0.7% estimate
- Healthcare segment organic revenue growth: +2.7% vs. +2.51% estimate
- Fabric and home care segment organic revenue growth: +4.8% vs. +2.35% estimate
- Baby, feminine, and family care segment organic revenue growth: +3% vs. +0.99% estimate
- Gross margin: 49.8% vs. 50% estimate
- Adjusted earnings per share: $2.00, +1% from the prior year vs. $1.89 estimate
What else caught our attention: A sustained outlook
P&G reiterated organic sales growth of 1% to 3% for its fiscal year.
For the year, earnings are still expected to range from $6.89 to $7.11. Analysts were looking for fiscal year 2027 organic revenue growth of 2.19% and core earnings per share of $6.98.
Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

item.title: Trump and Crypto Firm Sued for Profiting From Foreign Government
item.author: Bob Van Voris; Olga Kharif
item.description:
Trump and Crypto Firm Sued for Profiting From Foreign Government
2026-10-23
Por Bob Van Voris; Olga Kharif
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/trump-crypto-firm-sued-profiting-184013450.html
(Bloomberg) -- Donald Trump and World Liberty Financial, the cryptocurrency venture he co-founded with his sons, were sued by a shareholder in a rival crypto firm over claims the president illegally profited from his office in violation of the US Constitution.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Benjamin Greenberg, a shareholder in Circle Internet Group Inc., claims illegal competition from World Liberty has harmed him and other Circle investors financially.
The suit claims Trump violated the Foreign Emoluments Clause, a provision of the US Constitution that bars presidents from taking payments from foreign governments without the approval of Congress, in two World Liberty transactions with the United Arab Emirates.
"This action is about the President of the United States corruptly profiting from more than $2 billion in payments from a foreign government in direct violation of the Constitution," Greenberg said in a complaint filed Thursday in federal court in Washington. "No president in American history has profited from his office so brazenly."
Trump reported $1.4 billion in earnings related to his crypto ventures, including World Liberty, last year. 2026-10-23

Por Bob Van Voris; Olga Kharif

https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/trump-crypto-firm-sued-profiting-184013450.html

Most Read from Bloomberg

Benjamin Greenberg, a shareholder in Circle Internet Group Inc., claims illegal competition from World Liberty has harmed him and other Circle investors financially.

item.title: California's Prop 40: What to know about the billionaire wealth tax
item.author: Hal Bundrick; CFP
item.description:
California's Prop 40: What to know about the billionaire wealth tax
2026-10-23
Por Hal Bundrick; CFP
https://finance.yahoo.com/personal-finance/taxes/article/californias-prop-40-what-to-know-about-the-billionaire-wealth-tax-202611704.html
The California billionaire tax, Proposition 40, is finally coming to a vote on Nov. 3. The measure would levy a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of the state's billionaires. Two competing initiatives on the same ballot, Props 41 and 42, are backed by opponents of the tax, including billionaires.
If either garners more yes votes than Prop 40, it could keep the tax from taking effect.
The labor union Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West (SEIU-UHW) is spearheading the campaign for the tax on the state's ultra-wealthy to prevent hospital and clinic closures, protect healthcare jobs, and help fund K-14 public education and state food assistance programs.
Opponents, including Gov. Gavin Newsom, say the tax would fuel an exodus of wealthy company founders and investors, spark job losses, and further weaken California's economy.
Read more: How billionaires get away with paying less tax
What is the billionaire's tax?
Prop 40 would levy a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of billionaire state residents, subject to the asset restrictions noted below. Taxpayers could choose to pay the tax in five annual installments, with a 7.5% annual deferral charge on the unpaid balance.
Who would pay?
Billionaire residents in California as of Jan. 1, 2026, would owe the tax in 2027. That's an estimated 255 eligible taxpayers, according to data from Altrata, a wealth-intelligence firm, reported by the Wall Street Journal.
The tax proposal is not based on income — that's a loophole that allows billionaires to pay less in income taxes than the average American. Rather, the proposed California tax is based on billionaires' assets, including equity holdings, often in their own companies. The impact on the most wealthy would vary widely.
A half-dozen or more high-profile billionaires relocated out of state as news of the proposed tax rolled out last year, so the number may be slightly lower.
Those who have reportedly relocated include Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, though neither has said that their moves were related to the possible tax.
A Meta regulatory filing dated Oct. 21 said that founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg told a special board committee that he was considering moving out of the state to avoid the tax if it were passed.
The committee said it was "critically important to keep Mr. Zuckerberg in a leadership position with our Company and that he continue to reside in and manage the Company from our headquarters in California," and approved a special class of stock that he could use to pay any wealth tax due.
The tax's effect would vary widely. The Tax Foundation, a right-leaning tax policy nonprofit, projected that the tax would render Tony Xu, the founder of DoorDash, bankrupt, with a tax liability of $4.17 billion, unless he could challenge the initiative's valuation of his assets.
On the other hand, Jensen Huang of Nvidia would face a tax liability of more than twice that: $8.5 billion. He told Bloomberg that he's fine with that.
Read more: Where do millionaires keep their money?
Who sponsors it?
The California healthcare worker union, SEIU-UHW, launched the "emergency tax" initiative to offset possible healthcare staffing issues and service reductions at healthcare facilities. The union estimates a nearly $100 billion loss of federal funding over the next five years due to the passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
How would the tax be calculated?
Taxpayers and trusts with assets over $1 billion would be taxed on businesses, securities, collectibles, and intellectual property, but the tax would exclude real property and certain retirement accounts and pensions.
How much would it raise?

item.title: The Live Nation Empire That Music Fans Hate is at Risk of a Break Up
item.author: Leah Nylen
item.description:
The Live Nation Empire That Music Fans Hate is at Risk of a Break Up
2026-10-23
Por Leah Nylen
https://finance.yahoo.com/media-advertising/articles/live-nation-empire-music-fans-094529396.html
(Bloomberg) -- The Crowbar nightclub of Tampa, Florida never looked like much outside: a squat building with painted-over windows in a neighborhood where feral chickens roam brick streets.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Inside was where the magic happened. For 20 years, Crowbar's single, 300-person room served as a place to hear unknown artists before they broke or popular acts offering more intimate shows. Musicians as different as rock band OK Go, country's Kenny Chesney and indie-pop singer Chappell Roan graced its stage. A generation of local rappers honed their skills there.
On July 31, Crowbar closed its doors for the last time, beset by rising costs and the elephant in any discussion about concerts in the US: Live Nation Entertainment Inc. The colossus — which owns arenas and clubs, runs the nation's biggest ticketing service and manages musicians' careers — plans to build its own venue nearby. For Crowbar's final show, rapper Talib Kweli flew down from New York City, with local hip hop artists joining him onstage.
Across the country, some 480 independent venues and 240 music festivals have shut since 2020, with 160 shuttering so far this year, according to the National Independent Venue Association, a trade group for the industry. While the Covid-19 pandemic and surging inflation each played a role, so has the market power of Live Nation, according to Crowbar owner Tom DeGeorge and other independents. They struggle to compete against a $40 billion company that can steer artists to play one venue and avoid others while exerting significant control over ticket pricing through its Ticketmaster subsidiary.
This year, the Trump administration agreed to settle a monopoly case against Live Nation weeks after the company's CEO met with the president. The company denies any political interference. Displeased with the deal, a group of states fought on and, in April, won a landmark jury verdict that the company illegally monopolized live events. Now, those states want a federal judge to take the rare step of ordering a corporate breakup. Independent club owners and many musicians argue it's the only way to bring balance back to the market.
"If Live Nation wasn't the monopoly they were, I think all of our independent venues would have the ability to thrive much more," DeGeorge said in an interview. "When you have one entity that comes in that controls the entire ocean, nobody else gets to swim."
US District Judge Arun Subramanian in New York, who is overseeing the case and will ultimately decide on a breakup, missed a self-imposed deadline in late July to rule on Live Nation's bid to throw out the jury's verdict. Three months later, he still hasn't decided or scheduled next steps in the case.
Live Nation, which plans to appeal the jury's verdict, said in a written statement to Bloomberg that the live entertainment industry is both fragmented and competitive. Its operations across different parts of the industry allow it to invest in the music ecosystem at large while supporting artists, the company said.
"Small venues often operate on slim margins, and when faced with the broader economic pressures we are witnessing today, some fail," the company said. "But there is also significant new investment in small venues. Live Nation is not dominant. A large majority of shows we promote take place in venues we don't own — over 5,000 shows last year."
Ticketmaster is likely the best-known part of Live Nation, handling tickets for an estimated 86% of the US concert market and serving as the largest ticketing operator in the world. But the parent company and its many subsidiaries also dominate areas of live music largely invisible to fans.
Based in Beverly Hills, California, Live Nation has operations in 55 countries across Europe, Asia, Austr
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Meta erases its 2026 gain as investors punish Big Tech’s biggest spenders
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Meta erases its 2026 gain as investors punish Big Tech’s biggest spenders
2026-10-23
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/investors-are-punishing-big-techs-biggest-spenders-meta-is-the-latest-casualty-174236447.html
Apple (AAPL), Eli Lilly (LLY), and Walmart (WMT) have added more than $400 billion since chip stocks peaked in early October. Meta (META), Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), and SpaceX (SPCX) have lost more than twice that.
Meta is taking the hardest hit. The stock is down more than 8% on Thursday, erasing about $145 billion in market value and wiping out its gain for the year. It's on track for its second-worst day of 2026 and its third straight drop of 5% or more the day after earnings — a first since its 2012 IPO.
Meta is stuck in a 2-year box
Thursday's drop looks dramatic, but on a weekly chart, it barely registers. For about two years, Meta has bounced between roughly $500 and $800, from its April 2025 low near $485 to its August 2025 record close of $790.
Slipping below the 2025 close turns Meta red for the year. It doesn't change the trend. Only a break out of the box would.
The broader damage is hitting the AI spenders.
Nvidia (NVDA) alone has shed more than $600 billion since Oct. 6, according to Yahoo Finance calculations, as chip stocks broke a bear trap.
The bill for AI is coming due
Meta beat on revenue on Wednesday, with sales up 26% to $64.6 billion. But the company raised its full-year expense outlook and narrowed its capital spending plan to $135 billion to $145 billion. It also unveiled a new class of nonvoting shares it can sell to raise money.
"He's not going to have the cash flow to support it. So he's going to have to raise capital, both debt and equity," Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, said to Yahoo Finance in reference to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg.
Bond traders were already nervous. Earlier this week, the cost of insuring debt from Meta, Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet, and Microsoft (MSFT) climbed to its highest in months. Truist analysts wrote that Meta's AI investments "will take longer to generate returns."
The core business is holding up, though. Luria said Meta is "gaining share from Google," with ad sales growing in the 20s. And Zuckerberg told analysts that if compute efficiency keeps improving quickly, "Muse will be highly profitable over multiple years."
Watch for a weekly close outside the box. A move above $800 would be a breakout to new highs, while a close below $500 would open the door to a much deeper slide. Until then, the moves are just noise inside the range.
Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.
Follow Jared Blikre on X at @SPYJared or email him at jaredblikre@yahooinc.com.

Nvidia (NVDA) alone has shed more than $600 billion since Oct. 6, according to Yahoo Finance calculations, as chip stocks broke a bear trap.

The bill for AI is coming due

Meta beat on revenue on Wednesday, with sales up 26% to $64.6 billion. But the company raised its full-year expense outlook and narrowed its capital spending plan to $135 billion to $145 billion. It also unveiled a new class of nonvoting shares it can sell to raise money.

"He's not going to have the cash flow to support it. So he's going to have to raise capital, both debt and equity," Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, said to Yahoo Finance in reference to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg.

Bond traders were already nervous. Earlier this week, the cost of insuring debt from Meta, Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet, and Microsoft (MSFT) climbed to its highest in months. Truist analysts wrote that Meta's AI investments "will take longer to generate returns."

The core business is holding up, though. Luria said Meta is "gaining share from Google," with ad sales growing in the 20s. And Zuckerberg told analysts that if compute efficiency keeps improving quickly, "Muse will be highly profitable over multiple years."

Watch for a weekly close outside the box. A move above $800 would be a breakout to new highs, while a close below $500 would open the door to a much deeper slide. Until then, the moves are just noise inside the range.

item.title: Ozempic wave boosts US cobblers and tailors as Americans tighten their belts
item.author: Danielle Kaye; Alexander Marrow
item.description:
Ozempic wave boosts US cobblers and tailors as Americans tighten their belts
2026-10-23
Por Danielle Kaye; Alexander Marrow
https://finance.yahoo.com/small-business/articles/ozempic-wave-boosts-us-cobblers-060738387.html
By Danielle Kaye and Alexander Marrow
NEW YORK, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Lorraine Scott has spent at least $300 to tailor her pants and jeans since losing 60 pounds on weight-loss drugs over the past year.
US consumers taking weight-loss drugs like Novo Nordisk's Ozempic and Eli Lilly's Mounjaro have turned to cobblers and tailors as they try to save money while shedding pounds, motivated in part by a cost-of-living squeeze and rising out-of-pocket costs for the drugs as US employers increasingly drop GLP-1 coverage.
Over the past year, leather repairers have seen a spike in requests for their services due to rapid weight loss — not just for belts, but also for shoe and bag strap adjustments tailored to customers' trimmer bodies.
The uptick in demand for alterations underscores how weight-loss drugs are upending the retail sector, with some corners of the industry well-positioned to benefit while others struggle to adapt. About 11% of US adults are on GLP-1 drugs to lose weight, according to Gallup, forcing millions of consumers to look for affordable ways to revamp their wardrobes.
Cobblers Direct, an online shoe and handbag repair shop with 25 brick-and-mortar stores in Texas and a nationwide mail-in service, is seeing double-digit year-on-year growth in its belt-shortening business, said CEO Stephen Kelly.
The company, whose around 100 artisans will soon be operating from a new, nearly 30,000-square-foot warehouse in Austin, is now shortening as much as 500 belts each week, Kelly said.
Customers, he said, have been walking into the stores with five or six belts slung across their shoulder. After getting a few more holes punched in, some have asked to keep the extra flap of leather as a "badge of honor."
"They'll pull their belt out and show how long their belt originally was. And then they tuck it back into their waistline," Kelly said.
About 80% of GLP-1 users are living in clothes that no longer fit, waiting six months on average before buying anything new, according to a survey of more than 700 US adults using weight-loss drugs by telehealth platform Trimi. Jeans are the most disrupted article of clothing, the survey found, with 90% of users lamenting poor fit.

item.title: Big companies are rethinking 'out of control' AI spending — and turning to cheaper models
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Big companies are rethinking 'out of control' AI spending — and turning to cheaper models
2026-10-23
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/big-companies-are-rethinking-out-of-control-ai-spending--and-turning-to-cheaper-models-162837207.html
IBM (IBM) is calling attention to a growing trend among companies and their AI spending: They're keeping a closer eye on it.
"I think what we are seeing is that at least larger enterprises are becoming a lot more cognizant and a lot more aware of what the true ROI of all of their AI spend is," IBM CEO Arvind Krishna said during the tech company's earnings call on Wednesday.
"They are also getting worried if some of the AI spending is completely out of control with no real return," he added.
While hyperscalers have been ramping up capital spending on AI infrastructure and data centers, enterprise customers are increasingly turning to open-weight models, whose core components are public, as a more cost-effective way to implement AI.
"Our computation is that for an average large enterprise, you can get going with maybe two or three racks [of infrastructure]," said Krishna. "It gives you the ability to run those open-weight models currently, anywhere from 25% to 10% of the token cost of the frontier models."
Krishna noted that IBM's on-premises IT infrastructure is well-positioned for the shift, enabling the protection of intellectual property by running models locally or on private clouds.
Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk recently argued that the key metric defining the AI build-out isn't physical capacity or power, but the price customers are willing to pay for the computing power being built. The costs of AI tokens have also fallen sharply.
(Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)
Companies are willing to pay a premium for computing power if it helps them increase revenue, improve profit margins, or cut costs. But those benefits have yet to materialize at a meaningful scale, Sløk has argued.
Frontier AI developers OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) and Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) are responding to enterprise demand for more affordable models.
OpenAI introduced lower-cost mid-range additions to its GPT-6 model family in September. Earlier this month, Anthropic unveiled Claude Haiku 5.5, promising better performance at a lower cost than its predecessor.
Anthropic is on the march toward its highly anticipated initial public offering IPO with an S-1 filing potentially dropping as soon as Friday.
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

item.title: Oil prices top $113 on worries of Iran-US escalations after midterms
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Oil prices top $113 on worries of Iran-US escalations after midterms
2026-10-23
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/oil-price-gains-on-possible-escalation-of-iran-us-tensions-after-midterms-120738560.html
Oil prices rose on Thursday to their highest level since May amid growing worries over an escalation of the war in the Middle East after the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
Brent crude (BZ=F) topped $113 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate crude (CL=F) hovered near $100 a barrel.
The US and Israel have reportedly drawn up plans for renewed attacks on Iran after the elections next month, according to the New York Times, citing unnamed US officials.
The United States has ordered nonessential embassy personnel to depart Saudi Arabia after a series of attacks at the country's airports and oil fields.
President Trump has said he will not attack Iran before the midterms and has suggested that fuel prices will fall afterward.
The administration has been looking for ways to ease high energy costs ahead of November.
Higher energy costs are adding to expectations that the Federal Reserve will need to tighten further this year to curb inflation. The market fully priced in a 25 basis point Federal Reserve rate increase in December, while 89% of market participants believe officials will hold rates steady at their October meeting next week.
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

item.title: Bond traders are backing off Fed rate hike bets — here's what it means for mortgage rates
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Bond traders are backing off Fed rate hike bets — here's what it means for mortgage rates
2026-10-23
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/bond-traders-are-backing-off-fed-rate-hike-bets--heres-what-it-means-for-mortgage-rates-180507914.html
If oil is about to spark an inflation wave, the bond market hasn't heard about it.
Brent crude (BZ=F) is trading around $112 a barrel, more than 50% higher than before the Iran war began in late February. Normally, that kind of spike would have bond investors worried about inflation and pushing interest rates higher.
Instead, Treasurys are rallying on Thursday as stocks slide. The 10-year Treasury yield (^TNX) is on track for its biggest one-day drop in more than two years, slipping back below 5%. When bond prices rise, yields fall. That matters for anyone shopping for a home, because mortgage rates tend to follow the 10-year.
The Fed is back in focus
Behind the move is a quick change of heart about the Federal Reserve as long-term interest rates decline. The Fed meets next week, on Oct. 28, and investors have been bracing for it to raise rates to fight perceived oil-driven inflation.
Read more: How the Fed rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
Those bets are fading fast. Fed funds futures now put the odds of an October hike at about 5%, according to Bloomberg data. That's down from 15% on Wednesday and 37% at the end of September.
The outlook for December has shifted too. As recently as Wednesday, traders were fully priced for a hike by year-end. Now they see roughly a 75% chance.
Why bond traders aren't panicking about oil
Even with oil soaring, the bond market's inflation forecast has barely budged.
One way to measure what investors expect is the gap between regular Treasurys and Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities, or TIPS, which pay extra when prices rise. That gap, called the breakeven rate, says investors expect inflation to average about 2.4% a year over the next five years. That's the same as before the war started.
So why did yields climb so much this year? Almost all of it came from "real" yields, which is what bonds pay after inflation. That's a bet the Fed will keep rates high enough to stop oil from turning into lasting inflation, not a bet that inflation is about to take off.
Not everyone buys the market's calm. Bloomberg strategist Simon White argues breakevens are "mispricing" the oil shock.
What it means for mortgage rates
The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate fell to 7.32% this week from 7.40%, according to Freddie Mac. That's the first drop in two months, after a seven-week climb that took rates to their highest level since 2023. Before the war, rates were just under 6%.
Freddie Mac's survey doesn't capture Thursday's bond rally. If yields stay lower, mortgage rates could follow in the coming days.
item.content:encoded:
Bond traders are backing off Fed rate hike bets — here's what it means for mortgage rates

2026-10-23

Por Jared Blikre

https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/bond-traders-are-backing-off-fed-rate-hike-bets--heres-what-it-means-for-mortgage-rates-180507914.html

If oil is about to spark an inflation wave, the bond market hasn't heard about it.

Brent crude (BZ=F) is trading around $112 a barrel, more than 50% higher than before the Iran war began in late February. Normally, that kind of spike would have bond investors worried about inflation and pushing interest rates higher.

Instead, Treasurys are rallying on Thursday as stocks slide. The 10-year Treasury yield (^TNX) is on track for its biggest one-day drop in more than two years, slipping back below 5%. When bond prices rise, yields fall. That matters for anyone shopping for a home, because mortgage rates tend to follow the 10-year.

The Fed is back in focus

Behind the move is a quick change of heart about the Federal Reserve as long-term interest rates decline. The Fed meets next week, on Oct. 28, and investors have been bracing for it to raise rates to fight perceived oil-driven inflation.

Read more: How the Fed rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments

Those bets are fading fast. Fed funds futures now put the odds of an October hike at about 5%, according to Bloomberg data. That's down from 15% on Wednesday and 37% at the end of September.

The outlook for December has shifted too. As recently as Wednesday, traders were fully priced for a hike by year-end. Now they see roughly a 75% chance.

Why bond traders aren't panicking about oil

Even with oil soaring, the bond market's inflation forecast has barely budged.

One way to measure what investors expect is the gap between regular Treasurys and Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities, or TIPS, which pay extra when prices rise. That gap, called the breakeven rate, says investors expect inflation to average about 2.4% a year over the next five years. That's the same as before the war started.

So why did yields climb so much this year? Almost all of it came from "real" yields, which is what bonds pay after inflation. That's a bet the Fed will keep rates high enough to stop oil from turning into lasting inflation, not a bet that inflation is about to take off.

Not everyone buys the market's calm. Bloomberg strategist Simon White argues breakevens are "mispricing" the oil shock.

What it means for mortgage rates

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate fell to 7.32% this week from 7.40%, according to Freddie Mac. That's the first drop in two months, after a seven-week climb that took rates to their highest level since 2023. Before the war, rates were just under 6%.

Freddie Mac's survey doesn't capture Thursday's bond rally. If yields stay lower, mortgage rates could follow in the coming days.

item.title: Del expediente electoral al presunto lavado de activos: este es el origen y detalles del caso Laberinto contra Luisa González
item.author: Mario Alexis González
item.description:
Del expediente electoral al presunto lavado de activos: este es el origen y detalles del caso Laberinto contra Luisa González
2026-10-23
Por Mario Alexis González
https://www.primicias.ec/politica/luisa-gonzalez-andres-arauz-expediente-electoral-lavado-activos-caso-laberinto-135512/
Del expediente electoral al presunto lavado de activos: este es el origen y detalles del caso Laberinto contra Luisa González
El examen a las cuentas de campaña del binomio presidencial 2023 de Revolución Ciudadana, compuesto por Luisa González y Andrés Arauz, derivó en una sanción del Tribunal Contencioso Electoral y en la remisión del expediente a la Fiscalía, que indaga un presunto lavado de activos.
Momentos en los que Luis González fue detenido en Chone, el 22 de octubre de 2026, por el caso Laberinto.
- Foto
x / @mmendozabelen
Autor:
Actualizada:
Compartir:
Lo que comenzó como una revisión administrativa por inconsistencias contables de campaña ante el Consejo Nacional Electoral (CNE) siguió con una multa en el Tribunal Contencioso Electoral (TCE) y el envío del expediente a la Fiscalía; ahora terminó en la detención de Luisa González.
Diana Atamaint, expresidenta del CNE, denunció al binomio de Luisa González y Andrés Arauz por una infracción electoral. La acción se fundamentó en las inconsistencias detectadas en la omisión de USD 174.930 en propaganda electoral no declarada y USD 6.400 en aportes cuyo origen no contó con la documentación de respaldo requerida.
Tras la sentencia de la justicia electoral, el traspaso documental entre el TCE y la Fiscalía, mediante un oficio, originó la noticia del delito Nro. 170101826071336 por presunto lavado de activos, expediente en el que figuran cuatro sospechosos directamente vinculados a la Revolución Ciudadana.
A pesar de que las multas electorales fueron saldadas y la causa contenciosa fue archivada, el expediente penal avanzó con la detención de González, quien ahora está a la espera de la audiencia de formulación de cargos.
El oficio 080-2026 y el inicio del caso
La derivación de este caso hacia la justicia penal se concretó con la emisión del Oficio No. 080-2026-MSSD-WGOC, el 23 de junio de 2026. El documento fue suscrito por Mircka Sánchez, secretaria relatora del despacho del juez electoral Guillermo Ortega.
A través de dicha comunicación oficial, el TCE remitió las copias certificadas de la Causa Nro. 575-2025-TCE a la Fiscalía. La recepción en el Ministerio Público quedó registrada el mismo 23 de junio de 2026 para el inicio de las investigaciones.
Este traspaso dio origen a la noticia del delito, que fue ingresada al sistema informático de la Fiscalía el 14 de octubre de 2026 a las 13:12.
La causa fue asignada a la Unidad de Fiscalía de Administración Pública Nro. 4, en Quito, y fue catalogada bajo la figura penal de lavado de activos, con el Ministerio Público como denunciante.
En la ficha hay cuatro sospechosos: Luisa Magdalena González Alcívar, Andrés David Arauz Galarza, Estefanía Elizabeth Molina Freire y Joseph Santiago Díaz Asque, todos vinculados al proceso de la campaña presidencial correísta en 2023.
El proceso electoral
La base del proceso comenzó con el examen de cuentas presentado por el binomio presidencial de Revolución Ciudadana, durante las Elecciones Presidenciales y Legislativas Anticipadas 2023. El primer análisis técnico se recogió en un informe aprobado el 19 de junio de 2024.
Posteriormente, la Dirección Nacional de Asesoría Jurídica emitió un informe jurídico el 27 de diciembre de 2024. Estos insumos motivaron una resolución del CNE de febrero de 2025, concediendo 15 días de plazo para subsanar los hallazgos.
El 19 de febrero de 2025, la contabilidad de la campaña entregó un expediente de descargo compuesto por 209 hojas y un soporte digital en CD. Sin embargo, tras el análisis de los auditores electorales, las justificaciones presentadas no lograron desmontar la totalidad de las inconsistencias detectadas.
El examen final quedó plasmado en d
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Diana Salazar: “¿Qué era lo correcto, acomodarme a la tranquilidad de no incomodar o hacer lo que correspondía?”
item.author: Mario Alexis González
item.description:
Diana Salazar: “¿Qué era lo correcto, acomodarme a la tranquilidad de no incomodar o hacer lo que correspondía?”
2026-10-22
Por Mario Alexis González
https://www.primicias.ec/politica/entrevista-diana-salazar-libro-memorias-fiscal-casos-corrupcion-amenazas-135413/
Diana Salazar: “¿Qué era lo correcto, acomodarme a la tranquilidad de no incomodar o hacer lo que correspondía?”
La exfiscal general Diana Salazar presenta su libro 'Diana: Más allá de la fiscal', donde repasa su trayectoria judicial, los principales casos de corrupción y su visión sobre la justicia ecuatoriana. Además, cuenta detalles inéditos de lo que pasó mientras investigaba la corrupción.
Autor:
Actualizada:
Compartir:
En entrevista con PRIMICIAS, Diana Salazar, exfiscal general del Estado y actual embajadora de Ecuador en Argentina, presenta su libro 'Diana: Más allá de la fiscal'. La obra ofrece un recorrido por su trayectoria personal y profesional en la justicia ecuatoriana.
Desde su infancia en Ibarra hasta su traslado a Quito, Salazar resalta el valor de la educación promovido por su familia materna. Su ingreso a la Fiscalía General del Estado en 2001 inició un camino dedicado por entero al derecho penal.
Durante su gestión, lideró casos judiciales de gran relevancia como FIFA Gate, Odebrecht, Sobornos, Sinohydro, Metástasis, Purga y Plaga. En el libro responde a diversas críticas sobre sus causas, detallando la complejidad institucional.
La obra aborda, además, su paso por la UAFE y sus vivencias en la función pública. Salazar reflexiona sobre la lucha contra la corrupción y el crimen organizado en Ecuador y hace un llamado a la unidad nacional frente a las tensiones políticas.
La entrevista
Su infancia y su familia
¿Qué le motivó a escribir estas memorias?
Básicamente, lo que me motiva es dejar la verdad, dejar mi posición de posverdad, de cómo sucedieron los hechos y que las personas tengan la posibilidad de conocer a Diana más allá del cargo, quién es aquella persona que ejerció durante seis años la Fiscalía General del Estado.
A lo largo del libro se menciona mucho a su abuela, ¿qué significa ella en su vida?
Sí, puedo decir que mi vida ha estado caracterizada por la fuerza y la presencia de la línea materna. Ella es la madre de mi madre y fue quien, a mi forma de ver, cambió nuestra historia, cambió nuestro futuro, porque, pese a las limitaciones propias de la época y de su condición, tuvo la visión y el acierto de construir alrededor de la educación un futuro distinto para nuestra familia.
Tuvo esta posibilidad de que mi madre y mis tíos se puedan formar y que, a su vez, ellos vayan dejando ese legado que ahora yo quiero que para mis hijas sea también.
Otro de los puntos que se tratan en el libro es cómo eventos que han ido sucediendo en su vida han sido como una especie de motivos para seguir adelante, para cambiar, para dar un giro. El primero, tal vez la mudanza a Quito dejando Ibarra. ¿Qué recuerda de esa época?
Los aleteos, como los denomino en el libro. Yo creo que ese es un cambio que me ayudó a crecer. Yo no quiero hablar de fracasos o de éxitos, sino más bien de aprendizajes. Entonces, uno de los primeros aprendizajes fue tener que valerme por mí misma sin tener el acompañamiento o la ayuda que teníamos nosotros en Ibarra cuando éramos niños.
Pero también creo que ahí se fue formando y forjando esa figura de la mujer que tiene que salir adelante, en este caso, mi madre con mis hermanos, y que el único legado y la herencia que ella siempre nos decía era: Se tienen que formar, se tienen que educar para que puedan cambiar el destino.
Otra figura de la que se habla mucho y que nos ayuda a entrar en esta parte ya del derecho en su vida es la de su tío, que es quien la impulsa siempre a superarse, quien finalmente la conecta también con el mundo del derecho. ¿Qué nos puede decir de esa figura en su vida?
Y aunque él no sea propiamente un abogado, sino que fue esa figura o es esa figura paterna que no tuvimos dada la separ
[Transcripcion recortada]

2026-10-22
Por Mario Alexis González
https://www.primicias.ec/politica/entrevista-diana-salazar-libro-memorias-fiscal-casos-corrupcion-amenazas-135413/
Diana Salazar: “¿Qué era lo correcto, acomodarme a la tranquilidad de no incomodar o hacer lo que correspondía?”
La exfiscal general Diana Salazar presenta su libro 'Diana: Más allá de la fiscal', donde repasa su trayectoria judicial, los principales casos de corrupción y su visión sobre la justicia ecuatoriana. Además, cuenta detalles inéditos de lo que pasó mientras investigaba la corrupción.
Autor:
Actualizada:
Compartir:
En entrevista con PRIMICIAS, Diana Salazar, exfiscal general del Estado y actual embajadora de Ecuador en Argentina, presenta su libro 'Diana: Más allá de la fiscal'. La obra ofrece un recorrido por su trayectoria personal y profesional en la justicia ecuatoriana.
Desde su infancia en Ibarra hasta su traslado a Quito, Salazar resalta el valor de la educación promovido por su familia materna. Su ingreso a la Fiscalía General del Estado en 2001 inició un camino dedicado por entero al derecho penal.
Durante su gestión, lideró casos judiciales de gran relevancia como FIFA Gate, Odebrecht, Sobornos, Sinohydro, Metástasis, Purga y Plaga. En el libro responde a diversas críticas sobre sus causas, detallando la complejidad institucional.
La obra aborda, además, su paso por la UAFE y sus vivencias en la función pública. Salazar reflexiona sobre la lucha contra la corrupción y el crimen organizado en Ecuador y hace un llamado a la unidad nacional frente a las tensiones políticas.
La entrevista
Su infancia y su familia
¿Qué le motivó a escribir estas memorias?
Básicamente, lo que me motiva es dejar la verdad, dejar mi posición de posverdad, de cómo sucedieron los hechos y que las personas tengan la posibilidad de conocer a Diana más allá del cargo, quién es aquella persona que ejerció durante seis años la Fiscalía General del Estado.
A lo largo del libro se menciona mucho a su abuela, ¿qué significa ella en su vida?
Sí, puedo decir que mi vida ha estado caracterizada por la fuerza y la presencia de la línea materna. Ella es la madre de mi madre y fue quien, a mi forma de ver, cambió nuestra historia, cambió nuestro futuro, porque, pese a las limitaciones propias de la época y de su condición, tuvo la visión y el acierto de construir alrededor de la educación un futuro distinto para nuestra familia.
Tuvo esta posibilidad de que mi madre y mis tíos se puedan formar y que, a su vez, ellos vayan dejando ese legado que ahora yo quiero que para mis hijas sea también.
Otro de los puntos que se tratan en el libro es cómo eventos que han ido sucediendo en su vida han sido como una especie de motivos para seguir adelante, para cambiar, para dar un giro. El primero, tal vez la mudanza a Quito dejando Ibarra. ¿Qué recuerda de esa época?
Los aleteos, como los denomino en el libro. Yo creo que ese es un cambio que me ayudó a crecer. Yo no quiero hablar de fracasos o de éxitos, sino más bien de aprendizajes. Entonces, uno de los primeros aprendizajes fue tener que valerme por mí misma sin tener el acompañamiento o la ayuda que teníamos nosotros en Ibarra cuando éramos niños.
Pero también creo que ahí se fue formando y forjando esa figura de la mujer que tiene que salir adelante, en este caso, mi madre con mis hermanos, y que el único legado y la herencia que ella siempre nos decía era: Se tienen que formar, se tienen que educar para que puedan cambiar el destino.

item.title: Detienen a Luisa González, excandidata presidencial del correísmo en Ecuador
item.author: Santiago Sarango
item.description:
Detienen a Luisa González, excandidata presidencial del correísmo en Ecuador
2026-10-22
Por Santiago Sarango
https://www.primicias.ec/politica/luisa-gonzalez-detenida-manabi-caso-caja-chica-correismo-fiscalia-135484/
Detienen a Luisa González, excandidata presidencial del correísmo en Ecuador
La Fiscalía confirmó la detención de Luisa González, excandidata presidencial del correísmo, en el marco del caso Laberinto, que investiga presuntas irregularidades en el financiamiento de la campaña presidencial de 2023 y un posible delito de lavado de activos.
Fotografía de archivo de Luisa González, excandidata presidencial del correísmo en Ecuador.
- Foto
Autor:
Redacción Primicias
Actualizada:
Compartir:
Luisa González, excandidata presidencial del correísmo en Ecuador, fue detenida la madrugada de este 22 de octubre de 2026. El hecho fue confirmado por la Policía Nacional de la Zona 4 a PRIMICIAS.
Según información preliminar, la abogada, de 48 años, fue aprehendida en Canuto, cantón Chone, por agentes de una unidad investigativa de Quito.
En la madrugada de este jueves, el expresidente Rafael Correa publicó un mensaje en su cuenta de X en el que informó de la detención de González. "Apresaron a Luisa González. ¡Ya basta!", escribió el exmandatario.
Fiscalía habla del caso Laberinto
Pasadas las 07:00, la Fiscalía General del Estado confirmó que se ejecutó un procedimiento en Pichincha y Manabí con el fin de formular cargos contra tres personas investigadas por su presunta participación en el delito de lavado de activos.
El Ministerio Público agregó que la diligencia se desarrolla en el marco del caso Laberinto, que investiga presuntas irregularidades en el financiamiento político y el gasto en publicidad electoral durante la campaña presidencial de 2023.
Según la Fiscalía, en ese proceso electoral se habrían registrado inconsistencias en los aportes y en el origen lícito de los recursos.
En total, serían siete las personas investigadas en el caso Laberinto, entre ellas Luisa Magdalena González Alcívar, S. J. D. A. y E. E. M. F.
La detención de González se produce poco más de un mes después de que el Tribunal Contencioso Electoral (TCE) ratificara que no podía postularse como candidata a la Prefectura de Manabí.
Investigada por el caso Caja Chica
A inicios de 2026, González, quien fue candidata presidencial en 2023 y 2025, fue señalada en una investigación que apunta a la cúpula de la Revolución Ciudadana por el presunto delito de lavado de activos, en el llamado caso Caja Chica.
Según los expedientes, dinero de origen ilícito habría ingresado en efectivo desde Venezuela para financiar la campaña presidencial del binomio conformado por Luisa González y Andrés Arauz, en 2023.
Entre las personas investigadas figuran el expresidente Rafael Correa, el excandidato presidencial Andrés Arauz, la entonces presidenta de la Revolución Ciudadana, Luisa González, y otras figuras vinculadas al movimiento, como el exministro Fausto Herrera, el economista Patricio Rivera, la exsuperintendenta Suad Manssur, el asambleísta Patricio Chávez y la abogada Bibian Hernández.
En su momento, González intentó desvincularse de la gestión financiera cuestionada. Argumentó que, durante la campaña de 2023, su papel era el de candidata y que la responsabilidad administrativa recaía en Marcela Aguiñaga, quien entonces presidía la Revolución Ciudadana.
Como parte de las investigaciones, el 28 de enero de 2026, se allanó la casa de Luisa González.
En febrero del mismo año, la Fiscalía intervino la sede de la Revolución Ciudadana en Quito para recabar indicios relacionados con el caso Caja Chica.
Durante el operativo se recopilaron documentos, archivos y carpetas vinculados con los hechos investigados.
¿Quién es Luisa González?
Luisa González, de 48 años, cuenta con una trayectoria en el sector público, principalmente durante el gobierno de Rafael Correa, y una posterior participación en la Asamblea Nacional, donde ejerció como legislador
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Haung: ‘We have to accelerate AI safety’
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Haung: ‘We have to accelerate AI safety’
2026-10-22
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-we-have-to-accelerate-ai-safety-124206653.html
Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang says the AI industry needs to focus on safety following this summer's revelations that AI agents from leading labs broke free of containment and hacked into websites, including Hugging Face.
"It shouldn't have happened. Doesn't need to happen," Huang told Deirdre Bosa at Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference.
During his keynote on Wednesday, Huang revealed Nvidia's OpenShell Reference Architecture, which the company said will allow customers to build, contain, and observe AI agents. If an agent attempts to go rogue, Nvidia said the system can intervene and stop it.
"Hugging Face developed an exercise, a simulator, and they came to the conclusion: If OpenShell existed, their website wouldn't have been attacked that way," Huang said.
"We have to accelerate AI safety, and safety technology and capability to me is one and the same … As much as it is capable, you want it to be safe. The two of them are really one and the same. And so in the future, as we develop these AI capabilities, safety will come along with it," he added.
Part of that effort, the CEO said, comes down to establishing a zero-trust system around AI agents. Zero trust is a framework for protecting connected systems by limiting their exposure to other platforms and requiring people and platforms to regularly verify their identities.
Doing so, the thinking goes, reduces exposure to hacking and other cyberattacks.
"These agents are autonomous systems, and when you have an autonomous system on your computer … you should first start with zero trust, and give it minimum privileges, minimum access, minimum use of tools," Huang explained.
"Maybe they could access a file, but they can't delete the file. Maybe they can access the internet, but they can't … send stuff out," he added. "And so there are a lot of different things you could specify. Those practices about how to deploy agents and deploy autonomous systems [have] to be adopted across the board right away."
According to Huang, Nvidia is working with more than 100 companies to develop features to manage AI agents using OpenShell.
"We're working with all the labs and working with all the operating system companies. I think the [hacking incidents were] unfortunate, but I think that it's very much transformative for the industry," he added.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says data center builders have to be ‘good neighbors’
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says data center builders have to be ‘good neighbors’
2026-10-22
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-says-data-center-builders-have-to-be-good-neighbors-132705446.html
Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang says that for data center builders to win over communities, they must first partner with them and be good neighbors.
"When you go into a community … before you start building, you ought to extend yourself out to the local community and partner with them," Huang told Deirdre Bosa during the company's GTC event in Berlin.
"Let them know what you're about to do is going to bring, of course, all the benefits, but it's going to, of course, bring new neighbors," he said.
Data center construction has faced major pushback across the US, with some counties and towns instituting outright bans on the facilities. New York has placed a one-year, statewide moratorium on data center construction. Texas, meanwhile, has put connecting new data centers to its grid on hold as it works to determine their potential impact.
The issue has even become a flash point in the midterm elections, with President Trump backing data center development, and Democrats and some Republicans campaigning against them.
Residents have lodged complaints about the constant noise generated by data centers, water usage, increased electricity costs, and more.
To help ease tensions with local residents, some companies, including Microsoft (MSFT) and Amazon (AMZN), have taken steps to win over municipalities by dropping controversial nondisclosure agreements (NDAs).
NDAs have become a key issue among some data center opponents, as they prevent local leaders from disclosing information about the projects.
"Everybody has now taken a step back, whether it's the NDAs or contributing to the communities, whether it's building shops and … community centers and improving schools and in many cases even supporting lower taxes and, you know, all kinds of benefits that can be brought to the local communities," Huang said.
"I think those are all good ideas, and each one of them ought to be … tailored for the needs of the community. But the most important thing is you've got to be a good visitor. You know you should be a good guest. And before you go into a community, stop by and see if you can be helpful," he added.

item.title: Where people make over $1 million a year but still choose to rent
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
Where people make over $1 million a year but still choose to rent
2026-10-22
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/article/where-people-make-over-1-million-a-year-but-still-choose-to-rent-100000195.html
For even America's highest earners, renting can look more appealing than buying a home.
The number of renters in the US earning $1 million and up more than tripled between 2020 and 2024, according to RentCafe data, outpacing the growth in high-earning homeowners during the same period.
The data suggests that even the country's highest earners, while likely able to afford to buy if they wanted to, aren't immune to trends that have pushed millions of Americans to rent for longer. High mortgage rates still curtail their buying power, strong stock market performance makes tying up money in a home look less appealing, and renting can be a more flexible option than going through the process of buying and selling a high-end home.
Most $1 million-earning renter households are concentrated in the nation's priciest cities, where salaries tend to be higher and the cost differential between renting and owning often aggressively favors renting.
In New York City, home to more than 7,000 of these high-earning renters, a monthly rent of $15,000 to $20,000 — considered "comfortable" on that income by conventional affordability metrics — can cover a two- or three-bedroom apartment overlooking Central Park or a two-story unit in the trendy West Village. Buying a comparable unit, though, usually costs far more after factoring in high mortgage rates, taxes, and monthly maintenance fees.
San Francisco has the second-highest population of high-earning renters, with more than 1,800, followed by Los Angeles with 1,500.
But high-earning renters are increasingly popping up in small and midsize cities. Harrisburg, Pa., the state's capital, now has more than 140 renter households making over $1 million, up from just three in 2020. In Provo, Utah, the figure jumped from 10 to 264 in four years. Des Moines, Iowa, saw its highest-earning renters increase from four to 92 during the same period.
Most high-earning renters work in well-paying industries such as technology and finance or hold executive or managerial roles within their companies. About three-quarters of renter households bring in more than $1 million a year by combining two relatively high salaries, rather than having a single person rake in seven figures.
Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

item.title: Buffett’s Berkshire just trounced chip stocks and flashed a rare dot-com-era signal
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Buffett’s Berkshire just trounced chip stocks and flashed a rare dot-com-era signal
2026-10-22
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/buffetts-berkshire-just-trounced-chip-stocks-and-flashed-a-rare-dot-com-era-signal-165123739.html
For three weeks, Wall Street sold the hottest trade in the market and bought one of the oldest. Chip stocks lost 15% while Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway gained 7%.
That swing carried Berkshire's Class B stock (BRK-B) to a record close Tuesday, its first since May 2, 2025 — the day before Buffett said he would hand the CEO job to Greg Abel. The stock pushed to an intraday record Wednesday, as did the Class A stock (BRK-A).
The wait took 17 months, a stretch in which the S&P 500 (^GSPC) gained more than 35%.
From Oct. 6 through Tuesday, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) fell in 10 of 11 sessions. Berkshire rose on nine of those days, and on chips' two worst days, Oct. 14 and Oct. 16, it posted two of its best gains of the run.
For now, that price action has made Berkshire look like a hedge against the AI chip trade. Since Oct. 1, it has mostly risen on the days chips fell.
Berkshire is on track to rise in 14 of its last 15 sessions. Along the way, it strung together a 10-day winning streak, its first since 2018, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
A gap last seen during the dot-com bust
From Oct. 2 through Tuesday, Berkshire beat SOXX by 22 percentage points. That's the widest gap over any 12-session stretch since early 2010, according to Yahoo Finance calculations that compare Berkshire with the PHLX Semiconductor Index (^SOX) back to 1994. The 12-session window is the one that captures this month's widest gap.
The rarer signal is the combination.
Chips fell at least 14% while Berkshire gained at least 7% over 12 sessions. Before this month, that last happened Oct. 3, 2001. Every earlier case came in 1995-96 or in 2000-01, the latter as the dot-com bubble burst.
History sends a mixed message from here.
In the near term, chips bounced. They were higher a week later in five of the six earlier cases, and they're rebounding Wednesday,too. A year out, chips were lower in five of six instances, and the S&P 500 fell in four.
Four of those six cases came during the same bear market, though. Treat this as a rare signal, not a forecast.
Abel's Berkshire is spending again
Abel has also changed how Berkshire uses its cash. Berkshire bought back about $4.5 billion of its own stock in the second quarter and ended 14 straight quarters of net stock selling while its cash pile fell from a record $397 billion.
Buffett said Sept. 18 he would also step down as chairman. The stock bottomed two weeks later.
The next test comes with third quarter results, expected to be released Saturday, Nov. 7.

item.title: Nvidia reveals plans for 'an AI factory in a shipping container' to build data centers in weeks, not months
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Nvidia reveals plans for 'an AI factory in a shipping container' to build data centers in weeks, not months
2026-10-22
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/nvidia-reveals-plans-for-an-ai-factory-in-a-shipping-container-to-build-data-centers-in-weeks-not-months-125029004.html
Nvidia reveals plans for 'an AI factory in a shipping container' to build data centers in weeks, not months
Nvidia (NVDA) wants to reduce the time it takes for its customers to start generating revenue from its AI systems.
At its GTC event in Berlin on Wednesday, the company unveiled its DSX POD, a reference design for an AI data center packed into a box about the size of a standard shipping container.
Data center construction can take months, if not years, to get up and running. And because they don't start generating revenue until they begin processing AI tokens, the longer a data center takes to come online, the more expenses pile up.
The DSX POD is meant to serve as a faster, modular solution for companies that need access to data center capabilities sooner rather than later.
"The moment then you have to install these AI factories, and they're gigantic. And putting these AI factories into service takes months. If we could reduce that months, you know, from the moment that the systems are shipped to the moment that it's deployed and being operational, if we could reduce it from months to weeks or even a month, that will be completely game-changing for all of these AI factories," CEO Jensen Huang told Deirdre Bosa.
According to Nvidia, the Vera Rubin-powered DSX PODs will arrive on site, ready to be plugged into the power, cooling, and networking infrastructure, reducing deployment time from six months to 14 days.
The company said DSX PODs won't replace traditional data centers, but will serve as a means to start running AI applications before brick-and-mortar facilities are ready.
"With Nvidia DSX POD, we're bringing factory-built precision and speed to AI infrastructure construction — reducing deployment time from months to weeks so customers can scale capacity and bring revenue-generating production online faster," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement.
According to the company, the DSX POD supports liquid cooling, but because it uses dry-cooler designs, it can save up to 54 million liters of water per day versus a standard data center.
Standing up data centers more quickly doesn't just help Nvidia's customers, though. Faster data center deployment should ease at least one of the chokepoints in the AI build-out, which means faster chip sales for Nvidia.
Semiconductors aren't the only bottleneck for data center builders. Getting the electricity necessary to power those processors is also a concern. And power plants take far longer to construct than data centers.
Nvidia said it's working with partners, including Anduril, Armada, Bull, Crusoe, Dell Technologies (DELL), Foxconn, and others, to begin delivering the DSX POD in early 2027.
